# Actions

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/Actions.md

# Actions

Actions are configuration classes that define operations available in the admin interface. Each action class encapsulates settings and behavior for operations like viewing, editing, or deleting records. Actions are used to build the admin UI and handle user interactions.

- [Basic Usage](#basic-usage)

## Basic Usage

Actions are typically configured in your settings classes:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\ActionCollection;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\IndexAction;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\AddAction;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\EditAction;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\SettingsExt;

class UserSettings extends SettingsExt
{
    public function loadDefaultActions()
    {
        $this->withIndex();
        $this->withAdd();
        $this->withEdit();
    }
}
```

## Available Actions

### Core CRUD Actions

#### Index Actions
- [`DashboardAction`](#dashboard-action): Display dashboard tabbed indexes
- [`IndexAction`](#index-action): List index of records
- [`RelatedAction`](#related-records): Manage related records
- [`RelatedThroughAction`](#related-records): Manage records related through junction table

#### Form Actions
- [`AddAction`](#add-action): Create new records
- [`AddManyAction`](#add-many-action): Create multiple new records
- [`EditAction`](#edit-action): Modify existing records
- [`WizardAction`](Wizard.md): Wizard multi-step form interface

#### View Actions
- [`ViewAction`](#view-action): Display record details
- [`BriefViewAction`](#brief-view-action): Simplified view of record details

#### Delete Actions
- [`DeleteAction`](#delete-action): Remove records

### Special Actions
- `AutocompleteAction`: Handles autocomplete functionality
- `BulkAction`: Perform operations on multiple records
- [`CsvAction`](#csv-action): Export data to CSV
- `InlineEditAction`: Edit records directly in lists
- [`UploadAction`](#upload-action): Handle file uploads
- `TableActionsAction`: Actions for table rows

## Dashboard Action
Dashboard actions allow you to display tabbed indexes on a dashboard. This is useful for providing a quick overview of different data sets in single page.
By default, htmx is used in tabs for the dashboard to provide a seamless and dynamic user experience, allowing for efficient content loading and interaction without full page reloads.

### Example Usage

```php
use Cake\Database\Query\SelectQuery;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\DashboardAction;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\IndexAction;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\IndexLink;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\SettingsExt;

class UserSettings extends SettingsExt
{
    public function loadDefaultActions()
    {
        parent::loadDefaultActions();
        $cheapestAction = (new IndexAction())
            ->setTemplateizer($this->templateizer)
            ->setTemplateName('index')
            ->setName('cheapest')
            ->setQueryBuilder(function (SelectQuery $query, $key) {
                return $query
                    ->where(['budget <' => 100000])
                    ->orderBy(['budget' => 'ASC']);
            });
        $this->getActionsList()->add($cheapestAction);

        $expensiveAction = (new IndexAction())
            ->setTemplateizer($this->templateizer)
            ->setTemplateName('index')
            ->setName('expensive')
            ->setQueryBuilder(function (SelectQuery $query, $key) {
                return $query
                    ->where(['budget >' => 10000000])
                    ->orderBy(['budget' => 'DESC']);
            });
        $this->getActionsList()->add($expensiveAction);

        $dashboardAction = (new DashboardAction())
            ->setTemplateizer($this->templateizer)
            ->setTemplateName('dashboard')
            ->setName('dashboard');

        $dashboardAction->getTabsLinks()->add(
            (new IndexLink())
                ->setLabel('Cheapest Movies')
                ->setCrudLink('cheapest')
        );
        $dashboardAction->getTabsLinks()->add(
            (new IndexLink())
                ->setLabel('Expensive Movies')
                ->setCrudLink('expensive')
            );

        $this->getActionsList()->add($dashboardAction);

        return $this;
    }
}
```

## Action Configuration

Each action can be configured with various options:

### Common Configuration Methods
- `setName()`: Set the action name identifier
- `setType()`: Set action type (Based on Page constants)
- `setTemplateizer()`: Set the template handler for rendering buttons, links, page titles and subtitles, etc.
- `setProcessorClass()`: Set custom processor, or builder callable.
- `setFilterEnabled()`: Enable/disable filtering
- `setQueryBuilder()`: Custom query builder: used by all pages on first place.
- `setIndexFinder()`: Custom index finder: used by index/related/csv pages.
- `setGetFinder()`: Custom get finder: used by get queries in add/edit/view pages.
- `setCrudAction()`: Set the CRUD action type
- `setTemplateName()`: Set the template name for rendering
- `setTemplatePath()`: Set custom template path
- `setTemplatePrefix()`: Set template prefix for rendering
- `setTemplatePlugin()`: Set the plugin name for template resolution

### Display Configuration Methods
- `setTitle()`: Set page title (string or callable)
- `setSubTitle()`: Set page subtitle (string or callable)
- `setPageIcon()`: Set the icon for the page
- `setHelp()`: Set help text and configuration


#### Display Configuration Examples

- `title`: Set page title (string or callable)
  ```php
  ->setTitle('User List')
  // Or with callable
  ->setTitle(function($action, $entity) {
      return "Edit {$entity->name}";
  })
  ```
- `subTitle`: Set page subtitle (string or callable)
  ```php
  ->setSubTitle('Active Users')
  // Or with callable
  ->setSubTitle(function($action, $entity) {
      return "ID: {$entity->id}";
  })
  ```

### Processor Configuration
Configure custom action processing:

```php
->setProcessorClass(CustomProcessor::class)
// Or with callable builder
->setProcessorClass(function($controller, $settings, $table) {
    return new CustomProcessor($controller, $settings, $table);
})
```

### Behavior Configuration Methods
- `setLazyActions()`: Enable/disable lazy loading of table actions buttons
- `setForceHtmx()`: Force HTMX interactions for the action
- `setModal()`: Configure action to render in modal dialog
- `setUnlockFormProtection()`: Enable/Disable form protection for the action

### Data Configuration Methods
- `setPopulateAssociations()`: Configure which associations to populate
- `setExcludedFields()`: Set fields to exclude from display/processing
- `setTemplateElements()`: Configure template elements for rendering


### Index Action

The Index action is used to list records.

```php
$indexAction = new IndexAction();
$indexAction
    ->setLabel('List Users')
    ->setType(Action::TYPE_CRUD)
    ->setFilterEnabled(true)
    ->setProcessorClass(CustomProcessor::class)
    ->setIndexFinder(function($query) {
        return $query->where(['active' => true]);
    });
```

### Index Configuration Methods
- `setAllowRenderLayoutFields()`: Enable/disable layout field rendering
- `setRowOptions()`: Configure table row display options
- `setListElement()`: Set custom element for list rendering
- `setTableButtonsStyle()`: Configure style of table action buttons

### Pagination Configuration Methods
- `setDefaultPaginatorLimit()`: Set default number of records per page
- `setDefaultPaginatorMaxLimit()`: Set maximum allowed records per page
- `setForcePaginatorLimit()`: Force specific pagination limit
- `setInfinitePagination()`: Enable/disable infinite scroll pagination


## View Action

View actions allow you to display detailed views of records. This is useful for providing a detailed view of a single record.
View actions support tabs to organize different sections of content, similar to dashboard actions, using htmx for dynamic loading.

### Brief View Action

Brief view actions are simplified views of record details, typically used for quick information display.

#### Example Usage

```php
$viewAction = new ViewAction();
$viewAction
    ->setAssociations(['MoviesCasts', 'Genres'])
    ->setTemplateizer($this->templateizer)
    ->setGetFinder(function($query) {
        return $query->contain(['Tags']);
    });
```
- `setAssociations()`: Specify which associations should be loaded as tabs
  ```php
  ->setAssociations([
      'MoviesCasts',
      'Genres',
  ])
  ```
- `getTabsLinks()`: Contains collection of navigation tabs for the view
  ```php
  $viewAction->getTabsLinks()->add(
      (new RelatedLink())
          ->setRelatedTableUrl([
              'controller' => 'Movies',
              'action' => 'byGenres',
          ])
          ->setForeignKeyName('movie_id')
          ->setLabel('Movies')
  );
  ```
- `setGetFinder()`: Customize the query for loading the record
- `setTemplateElements()`: Add custom template elements to the view
- `setViewVars()`: Pass additional variables to the view template


#### Auto-Refresh Configuration Methods

View actions support auto-refresh functionality to automatically update content at specified intervals:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\BriefViewAction;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\ViewAction;

// Configure auto-refresh for brief view
$action = (new BriefViewAction())
    ->setAutoRefresh(true)  // Enable auto-refresh
    ->setAutoRefreshInterval(60); // Refresh every 60 seconds

// Or for full view action
$action = (new ViewAction())
    ->setAutoRefresh(true)
    ->setAutoRefreshInterval(30); // Refresh every 30 seconds
```

- `setAutoRefresh(bool)`: Enable/disable automatic content refresh
- `setAutoRefreshInterval(int)`: Set refresh interval in seconds (defaults to 30)
- `isAutoRefresh()`: Check if auto-refresh is enabled
- `getAutoRefreshInterval()`: Get current refresh interval

The auto-refresh functionality:
- Uses HTMX for seamless updates without full page reloads
- Updates only the view content
- Works with both standard and tabbed views

## Form Actions (Add/Edit)

The Form actions are used to create and modify records.

### Form Configuration Methods
- `setAutoPatchUserData()`: Configure automatic user data patching
- `setPatchEntityOptions()`: Set options for entity patching
- `setSaveOptions()`: Configure entity save behavior
- `setFormButtons()`: Set form button collection
- `setFormOptions()`: Configure form rendering options


### Add Action
The Add action is used to create new records.

```php
$addAction = new AddAction();
$addAction
    ->setTemplateizer($this->templateizer)
    ->setGetFinder(function($query) {
        return $query->contain(['Tags']);
    });
```

### Add Many Action
The Add Many action is used to create multiple new records.

```php
$addManyAction = new AddManyAction();
$addManyAction
    ->setTemplateizer($this->templateizer)
    ->setGetFinder(function($query) {
        return $query->contain(['Tags']);
    });
```

### Edit Action
The Edit action is used to modify existing records.

```php
$editAction = new EditAction();
$editAction
    ->setTemplateizer($this->templateizer)
    ->setGetFinder(function($query) {
        return $query->contain(['Tags']);
    });
```

### Form Action Properties
Form actions (Add/Edit) support additional configuration:

- `formOptions`: Configure form rendering options
  ```php
  ->setFormOptions([
      'type' => 'file',
      'class' => 'custom-form',
      'data-form' => 'ajax'
  ])
  ```
- `formButtons`: Customize form buttons collection
  ```php
  ->setFormButtons((new FormButtonCollection())
      ->add(new SaveButton())
      ->add(new CancelButton())
  )
  ```
- `saveOptions`: Configure entity save behavior
  ```php
  ->setSaveOptions([
      'associated' => ['Tags', 'Categories'],
      'atomic' => false,
      'checkRules' => true
  ])
  ```

### Form Buttons
Form actions use a collection of buttons that can be customized. Each button can be configured with various properties.

#### Button Types
There are three basic button types defined in `FormButton`:
- `TYPE_BUTTON`: Standard button
- `TYPE_SUBMIT`: Form submit button
- `TYPE_LINK`: Link styled as button

#### Available Button Classes
- `BackButton`: Navigation button with left arrow icon
  ```php
  new BackButton(__('Back')) // Default label is "Back"
  ```
- `SaveGoButton`: Submit button to save and return to index
  ```php
  new SaveGoButton(__('Save & Go')) // Default label is "Save & Go"
  ```
- `SaveViewButton`: Submit button to save and view record
  ```php
  new SaveViewButton(__('Save & View')) // Default label is "Save & View"
  ```

#### Button Properties
Each button can be customized with the following properties:
```php
$button
    ->setName('button_name')      // Form field name
    ->setValue('button_value')    // Form field value
    ->setLabel('Custom Label')    // Button text
    ->setType('submit')          // button, submit, or link
    ->setClasses('btn btn-primary') // CSS classes
    ->setIcon('fa fa-save');     // Font Awesome icon class
```

#### Managing Button Collection
```php
// Add single button
$action->getFormButtons()->add(new SaveViewButton());

// Add multiple buttons
$action->getFormButtons()->addMany([
    new BackButton(),
    new SaveGoButton(),
    new SaveViewButton(),
]);

// Remove a button
$action->getFormButtons()->remove('save_view');

// Get button names
$buttonNames = $action->getFormButtons()->keys();
```

#### Default Button Configuration
Common button configurations:
```php
// Back button
new BackButton()
    ->setType(FormButton::TYPE_LINK)
    ->setClasses('btn btn-secondary me-3 col')
    ->setIcon('fa fa-arrow-left');

// Save & Go button
new SaveGoButton()
    ->setType(FormButton::TYPE_SUBMIT)
    ->setClasses('btn btn-primary me-3 col')
    ->setIcon('fa fa-forward');

// Save & View button
new SaveViewButton()
    ->setType(FormButton::TYPE_SUBMIT)
    ->setClasses('btn btn-primary me-3 col')
    ->setIcon('fa fa-eye');
```

### Delete Actions
The Delete action handles record removal with optional soft delete support.

```php
$deleteAction = new DeleteAction();
$deleteAction
    ->setTemplateizer($this->templateizer);
```

### Configuration Methods
- `setGetFinder()`: Custom query builder for retrieving data before displaying the form
- `setAssociated()`: Specify which associated entities should be saved (`['Tags', 'Categories']`)
- `setSaveOptions()`: Configure entity save behavior
  ```php
  ->setSaveOptions([
      'associated' => ['Tags'],
      'atomic' => false,
      'checkRules' => true
  ])
  ```
- `setAutoPatchUserData()`: Auto-populate fields with user data
  ```php
  ->setAutoPatchUserData([
      'created_by' => 'id',
      'modified_by' => 'username'
  ])
  ```
- `setValidationSet()`: Set custom validation rules set (`'default'` or `'admin'`)
- `setRedirectUrl()`: Custom redirect after successful save (`'/admin/users'`)


## Related Records

For managing related records:

### Related Records Configuration Methods
- `setForeignKey()`: Set the foreign key for related records
- `setFilterBuilder()`: Set custom filter for related records

```php
$relatedAction = new RelatedAction();
$relatedAction
    ->setForeignKey('user_id')
    ->setFilterBuilder(function($query, $table, $action, $foreignKey) {
        return $query->where([$foreignKey => $value]);
    });
```

## Report Action

The Report Action provides a flexible framework for generating and rendering data reports in various formats (HTML, PDF, Excel).

### Basic Configuration

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\ReportAction;
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\Engine\PdfEngine;
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\Engine\ExcelEngine;
use App\Report\SalesReport;

// Create report action
$reportAction = new ReportAction();
$reportAction
    ->setName('sales_report')
    ->setLabel('Sales Report')
    ->setReport(new SalesReport());

// Add to actions list
$this->getActionsList()->add($reportAction);
```

### Report Engine Configuration

Reports can be rendered in different output formats using report engines:

```php
// Enable PDF engine with custom configuration
$reportAction->enableEngine('pdf', PdfEngine::class, [
    'engine' => 'CakePdf.WkHtmlToPdf',
    'download' => true,
    'margin' => [
        'bottom' => 15,
        'left' => 15,
        'right' => 15,
        'top' => 15
    ],
]);

// Enable Excel engine
$reportAction->enableEngine('excel', ExcelEngine::class);

// Disable HTML engine if needed
$reportAction->disableEngine('html');
```

### Report Action Configuration Methods

- `setReport()`: Set the report implementation to use
  ```php
  ->setReport(new SalesReport())
  ```
- `enableEngine()`: Enable a report engine for specific output format
  ```php
  ->enableEngine('pdf', PdfEngine::class, $config)
  ```
- `disableEngine()`: Disable a report engine
  ```php
  ->disableEngine('html')
  ```
- `isEngineEnabled()`: Check if an engine is enabled
  ```php
  $isEnabled = $reportAction->isEngineEnabled('pdf')
  ```
- `getEnabledEngines()`: Get all enabled engines
  ```php
  $engines = $reportAction->getEnabledEngines()
  ```
- `getEngine()`: Get an engine instance
  ```php
  $engine = $reportAction->getEngine('pdf')
  ```
- `getEngineForFormat()`: Get appropriate engine for format
  ```php
  $engine = $reportAction->getEngineForFormat('pdf')
  ```
- `setTemplateOptions()`: Configure template options
  ```php
  ->setTemplateOptions([
      'templatePlugin' => 'MyPlugin',
      'templatePath' => 'Admin/CustomReports',
  ])
  ```
- `setProcessorClass()`: Set custom processor class
  ```php
  ->setProcessorClass(CustomReportProcessor::class)
  ```

### Example with Report Registration

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\SettingsExt;
use App\Report\SalesReport;
use App\Report\InventoryReport;

class CustomersSettings extends SettingsExt
{
    // Constants for report identifiers
    const SALES_REPORT = 'sales_report';
    const INVENTORY_REPORT = 'inventory_report';

    public function loadDefaultActions(): void
    {
        parent::loadDefaultActions();

        // Register reports with default settings
        $this->addReport(new SalesReport(), self::SALES_REPORT);

        // Report with customized settings
        $this->addReport(new InventoryReport(), self::INVENTORY_REPORT, [
            'templatePlugin' => 'MyPlugin',
            'templatePath' => 'Admin/CustomReports',
        ])
            ->setLabel('Inventory Analysis');
    }
}
```

For more details about Reports, see [Reports Documentation](Reports/Index.md).

## Csv Action

### CSV Export Configuration Methods
- `setCsvFileName()`: Set the exported file name
- `setCsvFileExtension()`: Set file extension for export
- `setCsvFileType()`: Set the MIME type for export
- `setCsvDelimiter()`: Set the CSV field delimiter
- `setCsvViewClass()`: Set custom view class for CSV rendering

## Upload Action

### Upload Configuration Methods
- `setImportMethod()`: Set the method name for import processing
- `setImportConfig()`: Configure import behavior and validation


## Links and Buttons

Actions can have associated links and buttons:

```php
$action->getButtons()->add(new AddLink());
$action->getTableLinks()->add(new EditTableLink());
```

### Link Collections
Page actions can have multiple types of links:

- `buttons`: Top page action buttons
  ```php
  ->getButtons()->add(new AddLink())
  ```
- `tableLinks`: Row-level action buttons
  ```php
  ->getTableLinks()->add(new EditTableLink())
  ```
- `bulkLinks`: Bulk operation buttons
  ```php
  ->getBulkLinks()->add(new BulkDeleteLink())
  ```


### Available Link Types
- Regular buttons (`getButtons()`)
- Table row actions (`getTableLinks()`)
- Bulk actions (`getBulkLinks()`)

## Additional Configuration Properties

### Common Action Properties
- `isModal`: Configure action to render in modal dialog
  ```php
  ->setModal(true)
  ```
- `forceHtmx`: Force HTMX interactions for the action
  ```php
  ->setForceHtmx(true)
  ```
- `unlockFormProtection`: Disable form protection for the action
  ```php
  ->setUnlockFormProtection(true)
  ```
- `templatePath`: Set custom template path
  ```php
  ->setTemplatePath('Admin/CustomPath')
  ```


## Custom Actions

Create custom actions by extending base classes:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\PageAction;

class CustomAction extends PageAction
{
    public function __construct()
    {
        parent::__construct();
        $this->setLabel('Custom Action');
        $this->setType(Action::TYPE_CRUD);
        $this->setProcessorClass(CustomProcessor::class);
    }

    public function loadDefaultLinks(ActionCollection $actions)
    {
        // Add default links/buttons
    }
}
```

## Action Types

Two main types of actions:
- `Action::TYPE_CRUD`: Standard database operations

## Template Elements

Actions can include template elements:

```php
$action->setTemplateElements([
    Action::ELEMENT_PREFIX => 'prefix_element',
    Action::ELEMENT_POSTFIX => 'postfix_element'
]);
```

## Link Types

### Quick Overview
- Actions define available operations (e.g., edit, delete)
- Each action can have multiple link types:
  - Regular buttons (top of page)
  - Table row actions (in data tables)
  - Tab links (for navigation)
  - Bulk actions (for multiple records)

Actions use different link types to display operations:

### Button Links
Regular buttons that appear at the top of pages:
```php
// In an Action class
public function loadDefaultLinks(ActionCollection $actions)
{
    $this->buttons->add(new AddLink());
    $this->buttons->add(new IndexLink());
}
```

### Table Links
Actions that appear in table rows:
```php
public function loadDefaultLinks(ActionCollection $actions)
{
    $this->tableLinks->add(new EditTableLink());
    $this->tableLinks->add(new DeleteTableLink());
    $this->tableLinks->add(new ViewTableLink());
}
```

### Tab Links
Navigation tabs for different views:
```php
public function loadDefaultLinks(ActionCollection $actions)
{
    $this->tabs->add(new RelatedLink());
    $this->tabs->add(new TabLink());
}
```

### Bulk Links
Actions for operating on multiple records:
```php
public function loadDefaultLinks(ActionCollection $actions)
{
    $this->bulkLinks->add(new BulkLink());
}
```

---

# Links

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/Actions/Links.md

# Links

- [Overview](#overview)
- [Link Types](#link-types)
  - [Page Links](#page-links)
  - [Table Links](#table-links)
  - [Tab Links](#tab-links)
- [Link Collections](#link-collections)
- [Custom Links](#custom-links)

## Overview

Links in the admin panel are represented by classes that implement `LinkInterface`. Each link type provides specific functionality for navigation and actions within the admin interface.

## Link Types

### Page Links

Page links are used for primary navigation and actions in the admin interface.

In interface appearance, page links are displayed as buttons.

```php
// Basic page link setup
$link = new PageLink();
$link->setIcon('fa-list')
    ->setLabel('List Items')
    ->setCssClass('btn btn-primary')
    ->setCrudLink(Page::INDEX);
```

#### Available Page Links

| Link Class | Purpose | Default Icon | CSS Class |
|------------|---------|--------------|-----------|
| `AddLink` | Create new records | fa-plus | btn btn-success |
| `EditLink` | Edit existing records | fa-edit | btn btn-info |
| `ViewLink` | View record details | fa-file | btn btn-info |
| `DeleteLink` | Delete records | fa-times | btn btn-danger |
| `IndexLink` | List records | fa-list | btn btn-primary |
| `UploadLink` | Upload functionality | fa-upload | btn btn-info |
| `BackLink` | Navigation | fa-arrow-left | btn btn-info |

### Table Links

Table links appear in data grid rows for record-specific actions.

In interface appearance for tables, table links are displayed as buttons or dropdown menu items.

In interface appearance for other pages, table links are displayed as small buttons.

```php
// Example table link configuration
$link = new EditTableLink();
$link->setAppendReturnUrl(true)
    ->setUrlOptions(['class' => 'edit-record']);
```

#### Available Table Links

| Link Class | Purpose | Default Icon |
|------------|---------|--------------|
| `EditTableLink` | Row-level edit | fa-edit |
| `ViewTableLink` | Row-level view | fa-eye |
| `DeleteTableLink` | Row-level delete | fa-trash |

### Related Links

Links for handling related records and associations.

```php
// Related link example
$link = new RelatedLink();
$link->setRelatedTableUrl(['controller' => 'Posts'])
    ->setForeignKeyName('post_id')
    ->setMode(RelatedLink::MODE_FOREIGN_KEY);
```

#### Available Related Links

| Link Class | Purpose | Features |
|------------|---------|----------|
| `AddRelatedLink` | Add related records | Foreign key support |
| `RelatedBriefLink` | Quick view related | Modal support |
| `AddRelatedThroughLink` | Many-to-many relations | Through table support |

## Link Collections

Links can be grouped and managed using `LinkCollection`:

```php
$collection = new LinkCollection();
$collection->add(new AddLink())
    ->add(new EditLink())
    ->add(new DeleteLink());
```

### Collection Features
- Iterable interface
- Countable interface
- Add/remove links
- Bulk operations

## Link Configuration

### Common Properties

```php
$link->setIcon('fa-icon')        // FontAwesome icon
    ->setLabel('Action Label')   // Display label
    ->setCssClass('btn-class')   // CSS classes
    ->setMethod('POST')          // HTTP method
    ->setUrlOptions([           // URL generation options
        'confirm' => 'Are you sure?',
        'class' => 'action-link'
    ]);
```

### URL Building

Links support multiple URL building strategies:

```php
// Default URL builder
$link->defaultUrlBuilder($request, $entity);

// Related URL builder with foreign key
$link->relatedUrlBuilder($request, $entity);

// Custom URL builder
$link->setUrlBuilder(function($request, $entity) {
    return Router::url(['action' => 'custom', $entity->id]);
});
```

## Traits and Base Classes

- `LinkTrait`: Common link functionality
- `AddByForeignKeyTrait`: Foreign key handling
- `RelatedThroughLinkTrait`: Many-to-many relationship support

## Custom Links

Create custom links by extending base classes:

```php
class CustomLink extends PageLink
{
    public function __construct()
    {
        parent::__construct();
        $this->setIcon('fa-custom')
            ->setLabel('Custom Action')
            ->setCssClass('btn btn-custom')
            ->setCrudLink('custom');
    }
}
```

---

# Table Buttons Styles

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/Actions/TableButtons.md

# Table Buttons Styles

The Admin plugin provides 5 different representations for table row actions. These styles control how action buttons (like View, Edit, Delete) are displayed for each table row.

## Configuration Options

Two main settings control the table action display:

- `setTableButtonsStyle()` - Controls the visual style (none, inline, dropdown)
- `setLazyActions()` - Controls whether actions are loaded via HTMX (lazy) or rendered directly

## Available Styles

### 1. No Actions
```php
$indexAction->setTableButtonsStyle(IndexAction::TABLE_BUTTONS_STYLE_NONE);
```
Hides all row action buttons. Useful when you want to disable row-level actions completely.

### 2. Inline Actions (Default)
```php
$indexAction->setLazyActions(false);
$indexAction->setTableButtonsStyle(IndexAction::TABLE_BUTTONS_STYLE_INLINE);
```
- Displays action buttons horizontally in the row
- All buttons are rendered immediately
- Best for 2-3 actions maximum
- Most straightforward approach

### 3. Dropdown Menu
```php
$indexAction->setLazyActions(false);
$indexAction->setTableButtonsStyle(IndexAction::TABLE_BUTTONS_STYLE_DROPDOWN);
```
- Shows a dropdown menu button that reveals actions when clicked
- All actions are pre-rendered
- Better for many actions
- Saves horizontal space

### 4. Lazy Dropdown Menu
```php
$indexAction->setLazyActions(true);
$indexAction->setTableButtonsStyle(IndexAction::TABLE_BUTTONS_STYLE_DROPDOWN);
```
- Shows a dropdown menu button
- Actions are loaded via HTMX when the menu is opened
- Improves initial page load time
- Best for many actions with complex permissions

### 5. Lazy Inline Actions
```php
$indexAction->setLazyActions(true);
$indexAction->setTableButtonsStyle(IndexAction::TABLE_BUTTONS_STYLE_INLINE);
```
- Displays action buttons horizontally
- Actions are loaded via HTMX when hovering/focusing the row
- Balances visual clarity with performance
- Good for medium number of actions with complex permissions

## Best Practices

- Use inline styles for simple tables with few actions
- Use dropdowns when you have more than 3 actions
- Enable lazy loading when:
  - You have complex permission checks
  - The table has many rows
  - Actions are dynamically determined
- Consider mobile users when choosing between inline and dropdown styles

---

# AdminExtComponent

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/AdminExtComponent.md

# AdminExtComponent

The AdminExtComponent is a central component in the CakeDC Admin plugin that handles admin interface generation, processing, and management. It serves as the bridge between your controllers and the admin functionality.
It handles automatic CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations and supports custom action processing for specialized workflows. The component includes built-in modal support for dynamic content loading and integrates search capabilities for data filtering. The component also manages form handling with validation and provides authentication and authorization checks to control access to administrative features.


The main components and their relationships are illustrated in the following diagram.

```mermaid
graph TB
    Controller[Controller] --> AdminExtComponent
    AdminExtComponent --> SettingsExt
    SettingsExt --> ActionCollection
    ActionCollection --> ActionInterface
    ActionInterface --> Action
    AdminExtComponent -- "executes" --> Processor
    Processor -- "operates on" --> Table
    SettingsExt -- "configures" --> Field
    ActionInterface -- "uses" --> Field
    Processor -- "uses" --> ActionInterface

    subgraph "Action System"
    ActionInterface --> PageAction
    PageAction --> IndexAction
    PageAction --> FormAction
    FormAction --> AddAction
    FormAction --> EditAction
    PageAction --> ViewAction
    PageAction --> DeleteAction
    end

    subgraph "Field System"
    Field --> FormField
    Field --> DisplayField
    Field --> LinkButtonField
    end
```

The primary execution flow of the admin component is shown in the following sequence diagram.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Controller
    participant AEC as AdminExtComponent
    participant SE as SettingsExt
    participant AC as ActionCollection
    participant A as Action
    participant P as Processor
    participant T as Table

    C->>AEC: initialize()
    AEC->>SE: getInstance(table, action)
    SE->>AC: setup actions
    AEC->>AEC: beforeFilter()
    AEC->>AEC: _configureControllerForAdmin()
    AEC->>AEC: executeAdminAction()
    AEC->>SE: getCurrentAction()
    SE->>AC: byName(action)
    AC->>A: return action instance
    AEC->>AEC: _processAction(name, id)
    AEC->>P: new ProcessorClass(controller, settings, table)
    P->>A: getCurrentAction()
    P->>T: execute operations
    P->>C: set data for view
    AEC->>C: render result
```

## Basic Usage

Add the component to your controller:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Controller\Component\AdminExtComponent;

class MoviesController extends AppController
{
    public function initialize(): void
    {
        parent::initialize();

        $this->loadComponent('CakeDC/Admin.AdminExt', [
            'alias' => 'Movies',
            'settingsClass' => MoviesSettings::class,
        ]);
    }
}
```

## Configuration Options

| Option | Type | Description | Default |
|--------|------|-------------|---------|
| `alias` | string | Display name for the model | Table alias |
| `settingsClass` | string\|callable | Settings class or factory callable | null |
| `authCheck` | bool | Enable authentication checks | true |
| `slug` | string | Primary key field | 'id' |
| `table` | string | Table name to manage | null |

## Settings Integration

The component works closely with [SettingsExt](./SettingsExt.md) to manage:

- Field configurations
- Action definitions
- Processors
- Search behavior
- Form options
- Security settings

## Key Methods

### executeAdminAction()

Processes admin actions with proper context:

```php
public function customAction()
{
    return $this->AdminExt->executeAdminAction('customAction');
}
```

### isActionEnabled()

Checks if an action is available:

```php
$isEnabled = $this->AdminExt->isActionEnabled('index');
```

### getSettings()

Retrieves current settings instance:

```php
$settings = $this->AdminExt->getSettings();
```

## Modal Support

The component automatically detects modal requests through the `X-Modal-Request` header and adjusts the response accordingly.

## Security Features

- CSRF protection configuration
- Form security handling
- Authentication checks
- Authorization integration

## Related Documentation

- [SettingsExt Configuration](./Settings.md)
- [Action Processors](./Processors.md)
- [Field Types](./Fields.md)
- [Search Configuration](./Search.md)

## Events

The component triggers these events:

- `Controller.initialize`
- `Controller.startup`
- `Controller.beforeRender`
- `Controller.shutdown`

# Menu Builder System

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/AdminMenuBuilder.md

# Menu Builder System

The Admin plugin provides a flexible menu system for building navigation in the admin interface. The menu system is built around two main classes: `MenuItem` and `MenuBuilder`.

- [Basic Usage](#basic-usage)
- [Core Components](#core-components)
  - [MenuItem](#menuitem)
  - [MenuBuilder](#menubuilder)
- [Menu Configuration](#menu-configuration)
  - [Creating Menu Items](#creating-menu-items)
  - [Nesting Menu Items](#nesting-menu-items)
  - [Setting Icons](#setting-icons)
  - [Custom CSS Classes](#custom-css-classes)
  - [Dynamic URL Generation](#dynamic-url-generation)
- [Integration with Settings](#integration-with-settings)
- [Rendering Menus](#rendering-menus)
  - [AdminMenuHelper](#adminmenuhelper)
  - [Menu Search](#menu-search)
- [Extensions and Customization](#extensions-and-customization)
  - [Custom Menu Items](#custom-menu-items)

## Basic Usage

Here's a basic example of creating a navigation menu:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Menu\MenuBuilder;
use CakeDC\Admin\Menu\MenuItem;

// Create menu builder
$menu = new MenuBuilder();

// Add a main menu item
$menu->addItem(
    MenuItem::new('Dashboard')
        ->setIcon('fas fa-tachometer-alt')
        ->setUrl(['plugin' => 'CakeDC/Admin', 'controller' => 'Dashboard', 'action' => 'index'])
);

// Add another item with sub-items
$menu->addItem(
    MenuItem::new('Content')
        ->setIcon('fas fa-folder')
        ->addSubItem(
            MenuItem::new('Articles')
                ->setUrl(['controller' => 'Articles', 'action' => 'index'])
        )
        ->addSubItem(
            MenuItem::new('Categories')
                ->setUrl(['controller' => 'Categories', 'action' => 'index'])
        )
);
```

## Core Components

### MenuItem

The `MenuItem` class represents a single navigation item with properties such as title, icon, URL, and child items.

#### Key Properties

- `title`: Display text for the menu item
- `icon`: Icon class (e.g., Font Awesome icon)
- `class`: CSS class for the menu item
- `linkClass`: CSS class for the menu item link
- `url`: URL for the menu item (array or string)
- `subItems`: Collection of child menu items

#### Key Methods

- `new(string $title)`: Static factory method to create a menu item
- `setIcon(string $icon)`: Set the icon class
- `setUrl(array|string|null $url)`: Set the URL
- `setClass(string $class)`: Set the CSS class
- `setLinkClass(string $linkClass)`: Set the link CSS class
- `addSubItem(MenuItem $item)`: Add a sub-item
- `getSubItems()`: Get all sub-items
- `hasSubItems()`: Check if item has sub-items
- `toArray()`: Convert to array format for rendering

### MenuBuilder

The `MenuBuilder` class manages a collection of menu items and provides the structure for rendering.

#### Key Properties

- `items`: Collection of top-level menu items
- `menuClass`: CSS class for the menu container

#### Key Methods

- `addItem(MenuItem $item)`: Add a menu item
- `getItems()`: Get all menu items
- `setMenuClass(string $menuClass)`: Set the menu CSS class
- `toArray()`: Convert to array format for rendering

## Menu Configuration

### Creating Menu Items

Basic menu item creation:

```php
// Using constructor
$item = new MenuItem('Users');

// Using static factory method (recommended)
$item = MenuItem::new('Users');
```

### Nesting Menu Items

Create hierarchical menus by adding sub-items:

```php
$contentMenu = MenuItem::new('Content')
    ->setIcon('fas fa-folder');

// Add sub-items
$contentMenu->addSubItem(
    MenuItem::new('Articles')
        ->setUrl(['controller' => 'Articles', 'action' => 'index'])
);

$contentMenu->addSubItem(
    MenuItem::new('Categories')
        ->setUrl(['controller' => 'Categories', 'action' => 'index'])
);

// Add to menu
$menu->addItem($contentMenu);
```

### Setting Icons

Menu items can include icons (e.g., Font Awesome):

```php
$menuItem = MenuItem::new('Dashboard')
    ->setIcon('fas fa-tachometer-alt');
```

### Custom CSS Classes

Customize the appearance with CSS classes:

```php
$menuItem = MenuItem::new('Settings')
    ->setClass('nav-item settings-item')
    ->setLinkClass('nav-link settings-link');
```

### Dynamic URL Generation

URLs can be specified as arrays or strings:

```php
// Array format (preferred)
$menuItem->setUrl([
    'plugin' => 'CakeDC/Admin',
    'controller' => 'Users',
    'action' => 'index'
]);

// String format
$menuItem->setUrl('/admin/users');
```

## Integration with Settings

You can integrate menu generation with your `SettingsExt` classes for a modular approach using `SettingsExt::getMenuItem` method:


```php
$menu = new MenuBuilder();

// Movies Management
$menu->addItem(
    MenuItem::new('Movies')
        ->setIcon('fas fa-film')
        ->addSubItem(
            Movies::getMenuItem('dashboard', 'Movies Dashboard')
                ->setIcon('fas fa-list')
        )
        ->addSubItem(
            Movies::getMenuItem('index', 'Movies List')
                ->setIcon('fas fa-list')
        )
        ->addSubItem(
            Genres::getMenuItem()
                ->setIcon('fas fa-theater-masks')
        )
        ->addSubItem(
            Keywords::getMenuItem()
                ->setIcon('fas fa-tags')
        )
);
```

## Rendering Menus

The menu structure can be rendered in views using the `AdminMenuHelper`:

```php
// In a controller
$this->set('mainMenu', $menu);

// In a layout or view
echo $this->AdminMenu->render($mainMenu);
```

### AdminMenuHelper

The `AdminMenuHelper` provides built-in menu rendering functionality with proper accessibility features, collapsible navigation, and search capabilities.

#### Key Features

- Automatic rendering of menu items with proper HTML structure
- Integration with CakePHP's authorization system
- Support for collapsible, nested navigation
- Built-in search functionality for menu items
- Icon and styling support

#### Main Methods

- `render(MenuBuilder $menu, bool $includeSearch = true)`: Render the complete menu structure
- `renderSearch()`: Render the menu search input field

#### Example Usage

```php
// Basic usage in a template
echo $this->AdminMenu->render($menu);

// Render without search functionality
echo $this->AdminMenu->render($menu, false);

// Render only the search box
echo $this->AdminMenu->renderSearch();
```

The helper implements proper authorization checks through the `AuthLinkHelper`, ensuring that only accessible menu items are displayed to the current user.

### Menu Search

The `AdminMenuHelper` includes a built-in search functionality to filter menu items dynamically. When enabled (default), the helper:

1. Renders a search input field above the menu
2. Includes JavaScript for dynamically filtering menu items
3. Automatically shows/hides menu sections based on search matches
4. Expands parent menu items when a child item matches the search

This provides a better user experience for navigating complex menu structures:

```php
// The search box is included by default
echo $this->AdminMenu->render($menu);

// You can render only the search box if needed
echo $this->AdminMenu->renderSearch();
```

## Extensions and Customization

### Custom Menu Items

You can extend the `MenuItem` class to create specialized menu items:

```php
namespace App\Menu;

use CakeDC\Admin\Menu\MenuItem;

class BadgeMenuItem extends MenuItem
{
    protected string $badgeText;
    protected string $badgeClass = 'badge bg-primary';

    public function setBadge(string $text, string $class = null): self
    {
        $this->badgeText = $text;
        if ($class !== null) {
            $this->badgeClass = $class;
        }
        return $this;
    }

    /**
     * Get the badge HTML
     *
     * @return string
     */
    public function getBadgeHtml(): string
    {
        return sprintf('<span class="%s">%s</span>',
            $this->badgeClass,
            $this->badgeText
        );
    }

    /**
     * Get title with badge
     *
     * @return string
     */
    public function getTitle(): string
    {
        return parent::getTitle() . ' ' . $this->getBadgeHtml();
    }
}
```

Usage:

```php
use App\Menu\BadgeMenuItem;

$menu->addItem(
    (new BadgeMenuItem('Notifications'))
        ->setIcon('fas fa-bell')
        ->setBadge('5', 'badge bg-danger')
);
```

---

# Configuring Custom Fields in CakePHP Admin Plugin

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/AssetsConfiguration.md

# Configuring Custom Fields in CakePHP Admin Plugin

The CakePHP Admin Plugin provides a comprehensive system for registering custom fields and managing their associated assets.

## Field Registration System

At its core, field registration is handled through the application's configuration system. Fields are registered using the `Admin.assets.fields` configuration key, where each field class is explicitly defined. This approach ensures that the Admin Panel knows about all available field types and can properly preload assets using the AssetCompress plugin.

```php:config/bootstrap_after.php
Configure::write('Admin.assets.fields', [
    \CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\AutocompleteField::class,
    \App\Settings\Field\CustomField::class,
]);
```

Important note about plugin settings:

> Plugin setting `Admin.assets.plugins` are added for to transform CakePHP file paths to AssetCompress plugin format. If you have a plugin field, that uses assets from the plugin, you need to add it to this configuration.

## Asset Management

The asset management system handles both JavaScript and CSS dependencies for registered fields. Each field can specify its required assets, which are then automatically loaded when the field is used. This system handles asset loading.

```php:config/bootstrap_after.php
// Add custom assets
Configure::write('Admin.assets.js', [
    'custom-scripts.js',
    'plugins/datatable.min.js',
]);

Configure::write('Admin.assets.css', [
    'custom-styles.css',
    'plugins/datatable.css',
]);
```

## Integration Features

The system seamlessly integrates with CakePHP's plugin architecture, allowing plugins to register their own field types. Plugin assets are automatically resolved using the plugin's asset path, simplifying the development of modular field implementations.

# Using Admin Model Bake Command

For better model integration with CakeDC Admin, it's recommended to use the `admin_model` bake command instead of the standard CakePHP model bake. This command adds Admin-specific features to your models:

```bash
bin/cake bake admin_model -t CakeDC/Admin Users
```

This command will:
- Add hasMany associations for case when there is BelongsToMany associations

The `-t` or `--theme` flag specifies to use CakeDC/Admin's bake templates instead of the default ones.

# Baking Admin Controllers

To generate controllers optimized for the Admin panel, use the controller bake command with the CakeDC/Admin theme and Admin prefix:

```bash
bin/cake bake controller -t CakeDC/Admin --prefix Admin Departments
```

This command will:
- Create a controller in `src/Controller/Admin/DepartmentsController.php`
- Add necessary component configurations

## Controller Bake Options

### --prefix
Specifies the routing prefix for the controller (typically 'Admin' for admin panel)

### -t or --theme
Uses CakeDC/Admin's bake templates instead of CakePHP defaults

### Additional Options
```bash
# Generate with no actions
bin/cake bake controller -t CakeDC/Admin --prefix Admin --no-actions Departments
```

# Baking App Settings Class

The app settings class serves as a base class for your application's settings. You can generate it using:

Options:
- `--use-app-settings` - Use AppSettings as base class instead of SettingsExt
- `--search-type` - Type of search to generate (`default` or `filters`)
- `--search-association-as-text` - Use text search for association fields instead of select/autocomplete
- `--field-lists` - Type of list fields to generate (`select` or `autocomplete`)
- `--view-tabs` - Generate view tabs for hasMany and belongsToMany associations
- `--with-collection` - Comma separated list of hasMany association names to generate collection fields for
- `--with-belongs-to-many` - Comma separated list of BelongsToMany association names or "all"

````bash
bin/cake bake setting_ext AppSettings --use-app-settings
````

This will create `src/Settings/AppSettings.php` that extends `CakeDC\Admin\Settings\SettingsExt`. You can then use this as a base class for other settings by using the `--use-app-settings` flag:

````bash
# First create the base AppSettings class
bin/cake bake setting_ext AppSettings --use-app-settings

# Then create other settings classes that extend AppSettings
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies --use-app-settings
bin/cake bake setting_ext Users --use-app-settings
````

## Example AppSettings Structure

The generated AppSettings class will look something like this:

````php
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Settings;

use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\SettingsExt;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\Action;
use App\Settings\Action\AppViewAction;
use App\Settings\Action\AppAddAction;

/**
 * AppSettings base class for application settings
 */
class AppSettings extends SettingsExt
{
    /**
     * Override view action with custom implementation
     *
     * @param \CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\Action|null $action Custom action instance
     * @return $this
     */
    public function withView(?Action $action = null): self
    {
        $action = new AppViewAction();
        $action->setTemplateizer($this->templateizer);
        // Add custom configuration

        return parent::withView($action);
    }

    /**
     * Override add action with custom implementation
     *
     * @param \CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\Action|null $action Custom action instance
     * @return $this
     */
    public function withAdd(?Action $action = null): self
    {
        $action = new AppAddAction();
        $action->setTemplateizer($this->templateizer);
        // Configure custom redirect after save

        return parent::withAdd($action);
    }
}
````

This allows you to:
- Define common functionality for all settings classes
- Override default SettingsExt methods
- Add custom methods specific to your application

# Generate Settings for All Tables

Generate settings extension files for all database tables:

```bash
bin/cake bake setting_ext all
```

This command will:
1. Scan your database for all tables
2. Skip tables marked as skipped in your configuration
3. Generate a settings extension file for each table
4. Clear the table locator between generations to prevent memory issues

The command inherits all options from `bake setting_ext`, so you can use options like:
```bash
bin/cake bake setting_ext all --use-app-settings --search-type filters
```

# Bake Setting Extended Command

The `bake setting_ext` command generates settings classes for your CakePHP application.

## Basic Usage

```bash
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies
```

This will generate a basic settings class for the Movies table.

## Command Options

This addition helps users understand how to create and use an AppSettings base class in their application.


### --use-app-settings
Use `AppSettings` as base class instead of `SettingsExt`.

```bash
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies --use-app-settings
```

### --search-type
Type of search to generate. Options: `default` or `filters`

```bash
# Generate with default search
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies --search-type default

# Generate with filters search
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies --search-type filters
```

### --field-lists
Type of list fields to generate. Options: `select` or `autocomplete`

```bash
# Generate with select fields (default)
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies --field-lists select

# Generate with autocomplete fields
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies --field-lists autocomplete
```

### --view-tabs
Generate view tabs for hasMany and belongsToMany associations

```bash
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies --view-tabs
```

### --with-collection
Comma separated list of hasMany association names to generate collection fields for

```bash
# Generate collection fields for MovieCrews and MovieCasts
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies --with-collection "MovieCrews,MovieCasts"
```

### --with-belongs-to-many
Comma separated list of BelongsToMany association names or "all" to generate fields for

```bash
# Generate fields for specific associations
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies --with-belongs-to-many "Tags,Categories"

# Generate fields for all BelongsToMany associations
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies --with-belongs-to-many all
```

## Complex Examples

### Full Featured Settings Class
```bash
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies \
    --use-app-settings \
    --search-type default \
    --field-lists autocomplete \
    --view-tabs \
    --with-collection "MovieCrews,MovieCasts" \
    --with-belongs-to-many "Tags,Categories"
```

### Settings with Basic Search and Select Fields
```bash
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies \
    --search-type default \
    --field-lists select
```

### Settings with Advanced Filters and Autocomplete
```bash
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies \
    --search-type filters \
    --field-lists autocomplete
```

### Settings with Collection Fields Only
```bash
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies \
    --with-collection "MovieCrews,MovieCasts"
```

### Settings with BelongsToMany Fields Only
```bash
bin/cake bake setting_ext Movies \
    --with-belongs-to-many all
```

## Generated Files

The command will generate files in the following location:
- For application: `src/Settings/{Name}.php`
- For plugins: `plugins/{PluginName}/src/Settings/{Name}.php`

The generated settings class will include:
- Appropriate field types based on database schema
- Search functionality if specified
- Collection fields for hasMany associations if specified
- BelongsToMany fields if specified
- View tabs configuration if specified

# Additional Bake Commands

## Admin Model Commands

The admin model commands help generate model files with additional admin-specific features.

### Bake Single Admin Model
```bash
bin/cake bake admin_model ModelName
```

Features:
- Automatically adds `PlumSearch.Filterable` behavior
- Configures search fields for all columns
- Maps filter types (string -> Like, others -> Value)
- Disables BelongsToMany relations by default

### Bake All Admin Models
```bash
bin/cake bake admin_model all
```

Generates admin model files for all tables in the database.

## Action Command

Generate custom action classes for your admin interface:

```bash
bin/cake bake action MyCustom
```

Options:
- `--action` - Parent action class to extend from

Generated file: `src/Settings/Action/MyCustomAction.php`

## Field Command

Generate custom field classes for form handling:

```bash
bin/cake bake field MyCustom
```

Options:
- `--field` - Parent field class to extend from

Generated file: `src/Settings/Field/MyCustomField.php`

## Formatter Command

Generate custom field formatters for display formatting:

```bash
bin/cake bake formatter MyCustom
```

Generated file: `src/Settings/Field/Formatter/MyCustomFormatter.php`

## Processor Command

Generate custom processor classes for handling controller actions:

```bash
bin/cake bake processor MyCustom
```

Options:
- `--processor` - Base processor class to extend from

Generated file: `src/Controller/Processor/MyCustomProcessor.php`

Note: All commands support common bake options like `--plugin`, `--theme`, and `--force`.

# Settings Analysis

This is brief description of the `show` command. For more detailed information, see the [Show Setting Command](ShowSettingCommand.md) page.

## Show Settings Configuration

Analyze and display configuration details for a Settings class:

```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users
```

Options:
- `--action` (`-a`) - Show specific action only (e.g., index, add, edit)
- `--field` (`-f`) - Show specific field details (requires --action)
- `--only-actions` (`-o`) - Display only actions list in a single table

Examples:


Show only actions list:
```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users --only-actions
```

Show all configuration:
```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users
```

Show specific action:
```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users --action index
```

Show specific field in an action:
```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users --action index --field title
```

The command displays detailed information about:
- Action configurations
- Form buttons and fields
- Search configurations (@todo)
- Table links and bulk actions
- Field properties and options


---

# Best Practices

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/BestPractices.md

# Best Practices

This document outlines recommended approaches and patterns when working with the CakeDC Admin Plugin.

## Fields Definition

### Shared Fields Across Pages

If actions use the same fields for all pages, define them in `SettingsExt::fieldsBuilder(string $page)`:

```php
public function fieldsBuilder(string $page): iterable
{
    yield StringField::new('name')
        ->setLabel('User Name');
}
```

### Page-Specific Fields

If fields differ between pages, use conditional logic based on the `$page` parameter:

```php
public function fieldsBuilder(string $page): iterable
{
    if ($page === 'add') {
        yield StringField::new('name')
            ->setLabel('User Name')
            ->setRequired(true);
    }

    if ($page === 'edit') {
        yield StringField::new('name')
            ->setLabel('User Name');
    }
}
```

### Complex Field Builder Logic

For complex logic, use a match statement with separate methods for each page type:

```php
public function fieldsBuilder(string $page): iterable
{
    return match ($page) {
        'add' => $this->fieldsBuilderAdd(),
        'edit' => $this->fieldsBuilderEdit(),
        default => $this->fieldsBuilderDefault(),
    };
}

protected function fieldsBuilderAdd(): iterable
{
    yield StringField::new('name')
        ->setLabel('User Name');
}

protected function fieldsBuilderEdit(): iterable
{
    yield StringField::new('name')
        ->setLabel('User Name');
}
```

### Custom Application-Level Fields

When a field requires complex configuration, create a dedicated field class, especially if you'll use it in multiple places. You can then use it with `yield EmployerField::new('employer_id')` when initializing fields in the builder function:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\AutocompleteField;

class EmployerField extends AutocompleteField
{
    public function __construct(string $propertyName = 'employer_id')
    {
        parent::__construct($propertyName);

        $this->setAutocompleteUrl([
            'prefix' => 'Admin',
            'controller' => 'Employers',
            'action' => 'autocomplete',
            '_ext' => 'json',
        ])
        ->setQuery('employer_name=%QUERY')
        ->setValueName('employer_comparison.employer_name')
        ->setLabel('Employer')
        ->setSortPropertyPath('Employers.id')
        ->setDisplayPropertyPath('employer.id');
    }

    public static function new(string $propertyName, ?string $label = null): self
    {
        return new self($propertyName, $label);
    }

    public function showEmployerName(): self
    {
        return $this->setDisplayPropertyPath('employer.id + " - " + employer.employer_comparison.employer_name');
    }
}
```

## Search Definition

Define search fields in `SettingsExt::searchBuilder(string $page, ServerRequest $request)` to enable filtering in index pages.

### Application-Specific Search Fields

When a search field requires complex configuration, create a dedicated search class, especially if you'll use it in multiple places. You can then use it with `EmployerSearchField::new()` when initializing the search engine:

```php
namespace App\Settings\Search;

use Cake\Routing\Router;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Search\SearchField;

class EmployerSearchField extends SearchField
{
    public static function new(string $name = 'employer_id', ?string $placeholder = null): static
    {
        $field = parent::new($name, 'Lookup');

        $field->setParameterOptions([
            'autocompleteUrl' => Router::url([
                'prefix' => 'Admin',
                'controller' => 'Employers',
                'action' => 'autocomplete',
                '_ext' => 'json',
            ]),
            'idName' => 'id',
            'valueName' => 'employer_comparison.employer_name',
            'query' => 'employer_name=%QUERY',
            'wildcard' => '%QUERY',
            'minLength' => 2,
            'delay' => 300,
        ]);

        $field->setPlaceholder($placeholder ?? __('Employer'));

        return $field;
    }
}
```

## Extending Actions

### Configuring Existing Actions

You can configure existing actions using the `configureAction()` method:

```php
$this->configureAction(Page::EDIT, function (EditAction $action) {
    // Clear all buttons
    $action->getButtons()->clear();

    // Remove specific form buttons
    $action->getFormButtons()->remove('save_view');

    // Customize button labels
    $action->getFormButtons()->get('save_go')->setLabel(__('Save'));

});
```

Alternative way:

```php
/** @var \CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\ViewAction $viewAction */
$viewAction = $this->getActionsList()->byName(Page::VIEW);
$viewAction->setAssociations([
    'Users',
]);
```

### Adding Custom Actions

Use the `appendAction()` method to add custom view actions with specific processors and templates:

```php
// Add a custom view action with a specific processor
$this->appendAction(new ViewAction(), function (ViewAction $action) {
    $action->setCrudName('markAsPass')
        ->setProcessorClass(MarkAsPassProcessor::class);
});

// Add a custom view action with custom template and processor
$this->appendAction(new ViewAction(), function (ViewAction $action) {
    $action->setCrudName('qaFlow')
        ->configureTemplate('TestIterationCases', 'qa_flow')
        ->setProcessorClass(QaFlowProcessor::class);
});
```

### Global Style Configuration for Buttons

You can create a consistent look across your admin interface by defining global styles for buttons in an abstract base settings class:

```php
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Settings\Admin;

use CakeDC\Admin\Enum\Page;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\BaseFormAction;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\PageAction;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\SettingsExt;

/**
 * App Settings
 */
abstract class AppSettings extends SettingsExt
{
    /**
     * Button style mapping by action type
     *
     * @var array
     */
    protected static array $buttonStyles = [
       'back' => 'btn btn-subtle-primary',
        Page::INDEX => 'btn btn-subtle-secondary',
        Page::ADD => 'btn btn-subtle-success',
        Page::ADD_MANY => 'btn btn-subtle-success',
        Page::CSV => 'btn btn-subtle-primary',
        Page::UPLOAD => 'btn btn-subtle-primary',
        Page::VIEW => 'btn btn-subtle-primary',
        Page::EDIT => 'btn btn-subtle-success',
        Page::DELETE => 'btn btn-subtle-danger',

        'table' => [
            Page::VIEW => 'btn btn-outline-info mr-1',
            Page::EDIT => 'btn btn-outline-warning mr-1',
            Page::DELETE => 'btn btn-outline-danger',
        ],

        'form' => [
            'CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\FormButton\BackButton' => 'btn btn-subtle-primary me-3 col',
            'CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\FormButton\SaveViewButton' => 'btn btn-subtle-primary me-3 col',
            'CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\FormButton\SaveGoButton' => 'btn btn-subtle-primary col',
        ],
    };

    /**
     * @inheritDoc
     */
    public function initialize(): void
    {
        parent::initialize();

        $this->configureAction($this->getAction(), function (PageAction $action) {
            // Configure main action buttons
            foreach ($action->getButtons() as $button) {
                $type = $button->getCrudAction();
                if (isset(static::$buttonStyles[$type])) {
                    $button->setCssClass(static::$buttonStyles[$type]);
                }
            }

            // Configure table action links (for index and view pages)
            $actionName = $action->getCrudAction();
            if ($actionName === Page::INDEX || $actionName === Page::VIEW) {
                foreach ($action->getTableLinks() as $link) {
                    $type = $link->getCrudAction();
                    if (isset(static::$buttonStyles['table'][$type])) {
                        $link->setCssClass(static::$buttonStyles['table'][$type]);
                    }
                    $link->setLabel('');
                }
            }

            // Configure form buttons
            if ($action instanceof BaseFormAction) {
                foreach ($action->getFormButtons() as $button) {
                    $type = get_class($button);
                    if (isset(static::$buttonStyles['form'][$type])) {
                        $button->setClasses(static::$buttonStyles['form'][$type]);
                    }
                }
            }
        });
    }
}
```

This approach allows you to:
- Define CSS classes for different button types in a central location
- Apply consistent styling across all admin pages
- Easily update the look and feel of your entire admin interface
- Customize styling for main action buttons, table action links, and form buttons

# DebugKit Integration

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/DebugKit.md

# DebugKit Integration

## Table of Contents
- [Overview](#overview)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Admin Panel Features](#admin-panel-features)
- [Data Analysis](#data-analysis)

## Overview

The CakeDC Admin plugin integrates with DebugKit to provide detailed insights into your admin interface configuration, settings, and runtime behavior. This integration helps developers debug and optimize their admin implementations by providing real-time information about the current state of your admin panels.

## Installation

To enable the DebugKit admin panel, add the following code to your `bootstrap.php` or `bootstrap.local.php` file:

```php
$panels = Configure::read('DebugKit.panels') ?? [
    'DebugKit.Cache' => true,
    'DebugKit.Request' => true,
    'DebugKit.SqlLog' => true,
    'DebugKit.Timer' => true,
    'DebugKit.Log' => true,
    'DebugKit.Variables' => true,
    'DebugKit.Environment' => true,
    'DebugKit.History' => true,
    'DebugKit.Routes' => true,
    'DebugKit.Packages' => true,
    'DebugKit.Mail' => true,
    'DebugKit.Deprecations' => true,
    'DebugKit.Plugins' => true,
];

$panels = array_merge([
    'CakeDC/Admin.AdminSettings' => true,
], $panels);

Configure::write('DebugKit.panels', $panels);
```

## Admin Panel Features

The Admin Settings panel in DebugKit provides comprehensive information about your admin interface configuration. It displays details about actions, fields, widgets, and search functionality. The panel automatically updates as you navigate through different admin pages, showing relevant information for the current context.

The Action Analysis section shows information about configured actions including their CRUD operations, modal behaviors, and custom processor classes. You can inspect field configurations, display contexts, and validation rules through the Field Analysis feature.

The Search Configuration section reveals details about search fields, filters, and collection settings.

## Data Analysis

The analyzer component used both for building the admin panel and command line tool. It organizes information into clear, tabular displays.
