# Fields

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/Fields.md

# Fields

## Table of Contents
- [Overview](#overview)
- [Basic Field Types](#basic-field-types)
- [Special Field Types](#special-field-types)
- [Layout Fields](#layout-fields)
- [Common Field Options](#common-field-options)
- [Virtual Fields](#virtual-fields)
- [Field Collections](#field-collections)
- [Form Initialization Interface](#form-initialization-interface)
- [Presentation Fields](#presentation-fields)
- [Layout Generation](#layout-generation)
- [Field Formatters](#field-formatters)
- [Label Formatters](#label-formatters)
- [Field Extractors](#field-extractors)

## Overview

Fields are the building blocks of forms and views in the Admin plugin. Each field type provides specific functionality and rendering options. Fields can be used in forms, views, and other contexts. Fields can be rendered in CRUD pages, or in custom user defined pages.

## Basic Field Types

### Text Fields
- **StringField**: Basic text input
  ```php
  StringField::new('title')
      ->setLabel('Article Title')
      ->setCustomOption('renderAsHtml', true);
  ```

- **TextField**: Textarea for longer content
  ```php
  TextField::new('description')
      ->setLabel('Description')
      ->setDefaultColumns('col-md-12');
  ```

- **TextEditorField**: Rich text editor with Summernote
  ```php
  TextEditorField::new('content')
      ->setLabel('Article Content')
      ->setFormTypeOption('summernoteOptions', [
          'height' => 400,
          'toolbar' => [/* custom toolbar config */]
      ]);
  ```

- **EmailField**: Email input with validation
  ```php
  EmailField::new('email')
      ->setLabel('Email Address')
      ->setRequired(true);
  ```

### Numeric Fields
- **NumericField**: For integer/float values
  ```php
  NumericField::new('price')
      ->setLabel('Product Price')
      ->setInputType('number');
  ```

### Date/Time Fields
- **DateField**: Date picker
  ```php
  DateField::new('start_date')
      ->setLabel('Start Date');
  ```

- **DateTimeField**: Date and time picker
  ```php
  DateTimeField::new('published_date')
      ->setLabel('Publication Date')
      ->setDefaultColumns('col-md-4');
  ```

### Boolean Fields
- **BoolField**: Boolean/checkbox field
  ```php
  BoolField::new('is_active')
      ->setLabel('Active')
      ->setDefaultValue(true);
  ```

- **CheckboxField**: Alternative checkbox implementation
  ```php
  CheckboxField::new('terms_accepted')
      ->setLabel('Accept Terms')
      ->setRequired(true);
  ```

### URL Fields
- **UrlField**: URL input with validation and formatting
  ```php
  UrlField::new('website')
      ->setLabel('Website URL')
      ->setCustomOption('target', '_blank');
  ```

## Special Field Types

### [Builder Field](./Fields/Builder.md)

The [Builder field](./Fields/Builder.md) provides a flexible way to create dynamic content blocks with different types, fields, and formatting options. It's particularly useful for:


### File Upload
- **FileField**: File upload field
  ```php
  FileField::new('document')
      ->setLabel('Upload Document')
      ->setAccept('.pdf,.doc,.docx')
      ->setMultiple(true)
      ->setStoragePath('uploads/documents');
  ```

### Select Fields
- **SelectField**: Basic dropdown selection
  ```php
  SelectField::new('category_id')
      ->setLabel('Category')
      ->setOptions([
          1 => 'Technology',
          2 => 'Sports'
      ])
      ->setInputOption('empty', '-- Select Category --');
  ```

- **Select2Field**: Enhanced select with search
  ```php
  Select2Field::new('tags')
      ->setLabel('Tags')
      ->setOptions($tagsList)
      ->setMultiple(true);
  ```

- **AutocompleteField**: Autocomplete input with remote data
  ```php
  AutocompleteField::new('user_id')
      ->setLabel('User')
      ->setAutocompleteUrl(['controller' => 'Users', 'action' => 'autocomplete'])
      ->setIdName('id')
      ->setValueName('title')
      ->setQuery('title=%QUERY');
  ```

### SimpleTableField

The SimpleTableField provides a way to display tabular data from an entity's property. It's particularly useful for displaying arrays of records in a read-only table format.

```php
// Configure table columns
$tableColumns = [
    StringField::new('id')->setLabel(__('ID')),
    StringField::new('name')->setLabel(__('Name')),
    DateField::new('created')->setLabel(__('Created Date')),
];

// Create SimpleTableField
SimpleTableField::new('records')
    ->setLabel(__('Items'))
    ->setTableColumns($tableColumns)
    ->setShowHeaders(true);
```

**Key features:**
- Display data from entity arrays as formatted tables
- Each column can use any field type with their respective formatters
- Supports both array and entity records
- Customizable through template elements
- Reuses existing field rendering logic

**API methods:**
- `setTableColumns(array $columns)`: Set the columns for the table
- `addTableColumn(FieldInterface $field)`: Add a single column to the table
- `getTableColumns()`: Get the defined table columns
- `setShowHeaders(bool $showHeaders)`: Show or hide table headers (default: false)
- `setSourceProperty(Closure $sourceProperty)`: Set a custom callback for retrieving data
- `setTableElement(string $tableElement)`: Set custom element template (default: 'CakeDC/Admin.Field/simple_table')

**Example usage with nested data:**
```php
// Field definition
yield SimpleTableField::new('order_items')
    ->setLabel(__('Order Items'))
    ->setTableColumns([
        StringField::new('product_name')->setLabel(__('Product')),
        NumericField::new('quantity')->setLabel(__('Qty')),
        NumericField::new('price')->setLabel(__('Price')),
        NumericField::new('total')->setLabel(__('Total')),
    ]);
```

**Custom data source example:**
```php
// Using a callback to provide data
yield SimpleTableField::new('order_stats')
    ->setLabel(__('Order Stats'))
    ->setSourceProperty(function ($entity) {
        return $entity->getOrderStats();
    })
    ->setTableColumns([
        StringField::new('month')->setLabel(__('Month')),
        NumericField::new('count')->setLabel(__('Orders')),
        NumericField::new('revenue')->setLabel(__('Revenue')),
    ]);
```

**Customizing the template:**
You can override the rendering by creating an element at `templates/plugin/CakeDC/Admin/element/Field/simple_table.php` in your application or specify a custom element path using `setTableElement()`.

### ActiveSimpleTableField

The ActiveSimpleTableField extends the SimpleTableField to add interactive features like action buttons for each row and top action buttons for operations like adding new related records.

```php
// Configure table columns
$tableColumns = [
    StringField::new('id')->setLabel(__('ID')),
    StringField::new('name')->setLabel(__('Name')),
    DateField::new('created')->setLabel(__('Created Date')),
];

// Create ActiveSimpleTableField with actions
ActiveSimpleTableField::new('institutions')
    ->setLabel(__('Institutions'))
    ->setTableColumns($tableColumns)
    ->setShowHeaders(true)
    ->setRelatedModel('Institutions')
    ->setForeignKey('professor_id')
    ->addDefaultAddAction()
    ->addDefaultTableActions();
```

**Key features:**
- All features of SimpleTableField
- Row action buttons for operations like edit and delete
- Top action buttons for operations like adding new records
- Configurable related model and foreign key for proper linking

**Additional API methods:**
- `setRelatedModel(string $modelName)`: Set the related model name for link generation
- `setForeignKey(string $foreignKey)`: Set the foreign key field for relationships
- `addDefaultTableActions()`: Add default edit and delete buttons to each row
- `addTableAction(TableLink $action)`: Add a custom table action to rows
- `setTableActions(array $actions)`: Set all table row actions
- `getTableActions()`: Get all table row actions
- `addDefaultAddAction()`: Add default "Add New" button at the top
- `addTopAction(PageLink $action)`: Add a custom top action button
- `setTopActions(array $actions)`: Set all top action buttons
- `getTopActions()`: Get all top action buttons

**Example usage for institutions table:**
```php
// Field definition for professor's institutions
yield ActiveSimpleTableField::new('institutions')
    ->setLabel(__('Institutions'))
    ->setTableColumns([
        StringField::new('name')->setLabel(__('Institution')),
        StringField::new('department')->setLabel(__('Department')),
        StringField::new('position')->setLabel(__('Position')),
    ])
    ->setShowHeaders(true)
    ->setRelatedModel('Institutions')
    ->setForeignKey('professor_id')
    ->addDefaultAddAction()
    ->addDefaultTableActions();
```

**Custom actions example:**
```php
// Custom top action
$addLink = new AddRelatedLink();
$addLink->setLabel(__('Add Institution'));
$addLink->setCssClass('btn btn-primary');

// Custom row action
$viewLink = new ViewTableLink();
$viewLink->setLabel(__('View Details'));

yield ActiveSimpleTableField::new('institutions')
    ->setLabel(__('Institutions'))
    ->setTableColumns($columns)
    ->setRelatedModel('Institutions')
    ->addTopAction($addLink)
    ->addTableAction($viewLink)
    ->addTableAction(new EditTableLink())
    ->addTableAction(new DeleteRelatedTableLink());
```

**Customizing the template:**
You can override the rendering by creating an element at `templates/plugin/CakeDC/Admin/element/Field/active_simple_table.php` in your application or specify a custom element path using `setTableElement()`.

### Relationship Fields
- **BelongsToManyField**: Many-to-many relationship field
  ```php
  BelongsToManyField::new('tags')
      ->setLabel('Tags')
      ->setValueField('id')
      ->setLabelField('name')
      ->allowCreate(true);
  ```

### Collection Fields
- **CollectionField**: Collection of sub-fields
  ```php
  CollectionField::new('items')
      ->setLabel('Items')
      ->setNestedName('movies_crew_fields')
      ->addNestedField(
          StringField::new('title')
      )
      ->addNestedField(
          TextField::new('description')
      )
      ->addNestedField(
          BoolField::new('is_active')
      )
      ->addNestedField(
          HiddenField::new('id')
      )
      ->setMin(1)
      ->setMax(5)
      ->setAllowAdd(true)
      ->setAllowDelete(true);
  ```

Collection fields allow managing arrays of sub-fields. They support:
- Adding/removing items dynamically
- Configuring minimum/maximum items
- Optional sorting capability
- Custom add button label
- Nested field definitions

Api methods:
- `setMin(int $min)`: Set minimum number of items.
- `setMax(int $max)`: Set maximum number of items.
- `setAllowAdd(bool $allowAdd)`: Allow adding new items.
- `setAllowDelete(bool $allowDelete)`: Allow deleting items.
- `setNestedName(string $nestedName)`: Set nested name.
- `addNestedField(FieldInterface $field)`: Add nested field.
- `setNestedFields(array $nestedFields)`: Set nested fields.

### Counter Field

The Counter field is a special field type that is used to display a counter in the index page. It is useful for displaying a row number counter in a table.

- **CounterField**: Counter field
  ```php
  CounterField::new('_index')
      ->setLabel(__('#'));
  ```

### Hidden Fields
- **HiddenField**: Hidden input field
  ```php
  HiddenField::new('id')
      ->setValue($entityId);

### Key Value Field

Key value fields are used to display key value pairs in a table format. It accepts entity property with array value. This field type could be used for displaying configuration options, or other key value pairs like a list of countries, states, or translations.


- **KeyValueField**: Key value pair field
  ```php
  KeyValueField::new('key_value')
      ->setLabel('Key Value')
      ->setAllowAdd(true)
      ->setAllowDelete(true)
      ->setEditableKeys(true)
      ->setEditableValues(true)
      ->setReorderable(false)
      ->setKeyLabel(__('Key'))
      ->setValueLabel(__('Value'));
  ```

Api methods:
- `setAllowAdd(bool $allowAdd)`: Allow adding new key value pairs.
- `setAllowDelete(bool $allowDelete)`: Allow deleting key value pairs.
- `setEditableKeys(bool $editableKeys)`: Allow editing the key of the key value pair.
- `setEditableValues(bool $editableValues)`: Allow editing the value of the key value pair.
- `setKeyLabel(string $keyLabel)`: Label for the key field.
- `setValueLabel(string $valueLabel)`: Label for the value field.
- `setReorderable(bool $reorderable)`: Allow reordering the key value pairs.
- `setKeyPlaceholder(string $keyPlaceholder)`: Placeholder for the key field.
- `setValuePlaceholder(string $valuePlaceholder)`: Placeholder for the value field.


### Link Buttons
- **LinkButtonField**: Clickable button/link
  ```php
  LinkButtonField::new(
      Link::new('View Details')
          ->setUrl(['action' => 'view', $id])
          ->setIcon('eye')
  );
  ```

### Raw Content
- **RawField**: Raw HTML content
  ```php
  RawField::new('<div class="custom-content">...</div>');
  ```

### [Widget Field](./Fields/WidgetField.md)
- **WidgetField**: Base field type for displaying dynamic data visualizations and statistics. Includes:
  - [Stat Widget](./Fields/WidgetField.md#stat-widget): Single metric
  - [Chart Widget](./Fields/WidgetField.md#chart-widget): Interactive charts (line, pie, doughnut, etc.)

## Layout Fields

Layout fields help organize form structure:

### Panels
```php
// Basic panel
yield FormField::addPanel('Contact Information')
    ->setIcon('user')
    ->setCollapsible(true)        // Make panel collapsible
    ->setCollapsed(false)         // Set initial collapsed state
    ->setBorderless(false)        // Configure panel borders
    ->withBorders();              // Alternative way to add borders
```

### Fieldsets
```php
// Basic fieldset
yield FormField::addFieldset('Personal Information')
    ->setIcon('user')             // Add icon to fieldset title
    ->setCollapsible(true)        // Make fieldset collapsible
    ->setCollapsed(false)         // Set initial collapsed state
    ->setBorderless(true);        // Remove borders from fieldset
```

### Columns
```php
// Column with numeric width (6/12)
yield FormField::addColumn(6)
    ->setLabel('Left Column');

// Column with custom Bootstrap classes
yield FormField::addColumn('col-md-8 offset-md-2');
```

### Tabs
```php
// Basic tab
yield FormField::addTab('Details')
    ->setIcon('info-circle');

// Dynamic tab with HTMX
yield FormField::addTab('Related Items')
    ->setCustomOption(FormField::OPTION_TAB_IS_HTMX, true)
    ->setCustomOption(FormField::OPTION_TAB_HTMX_URL, [
        'action' => 'relatedItems',
        'id' => $entity->id
    ]);
```

### Rows
```php
// Default row (no specific breakpoint)
yield FormField::addRow()
    ->addCssClass('custom-row');

// Row with medium breakpoint (columns stack on screens smaller than md)
yield FormField::addRow('md');
```

## Common Field Options

All fields inherit these common methods from FieldTrait:

### Basic Configuration
```php
$field
    ->setLabel('Field Label')                    // Set field label
    ->setProperty('fieldName')                   // Set the property name/path
    ->setDisplayPropertyPath('model.field')      // Set custom display property path
    ->setHelp('Help text shown below field')     // Set help text
    ->setDefaultValue('default')                 // Set default value
    ->setValue('current value')                  // Set current value
    ->setInputType('text')                       // Set HTML input type
    ->setTranslationEnabled(true) // Set field translated
    ->setVirtual(true);                         // Mark as virtual field
```

### Display Control
```php
$field
    // Page Display
    ->hideOn(Page::INDEX)                        // Hide on specific page
    ->showOn(Page::ADD)                          // Show only on specific page
    ->hideOnIndex()                              // Hide on index page
    ->onlyIndex()                                // Show only on index page
    ->onlyViews()                                // Show only on view pages
    ->onlyAdd()                                  // Show only on add page
    ->onlyEdit()                                 // Show only on edit page
    ->onlyForms()                                // Show only on forms

    // Visibility & State
    ->setEditable(true)                          // Make field editable
    ->setRequired(true)                          // Make field required
    ->setUnlocked(true)                          // Unlock field for form protection
    ->setIsFile(true);                           // Mark as file field
```

### Styling & Layout
```php
$field
    // CSS Classes
    ->addCssClass('custom-class')                // Add CSS class
    ->setCssClass('replace-all-classes')         // Set/replace all CSS classes

    // Column Layout
    ->setDefaultColumns('col-md-6')              // Set default Bootstrap columns
    ->setColumns('col-lg-4')                     // Override column classes

    // Text Alignment
    ->setTextAlign('center')                     // Set text alignment

    // Sorting
    ->setSortable(true)                          // Enable/disable sorting
    ->setSortPropertyPath('custom.sort.path');   // Set custom sort path
```

### Form & Input Options
```php
$field
    // Input Options
    ->setInputOption('placeholder', 'Enter value')    // Set single input option
    ->setInputOptions([                               // Set multiple input options
        'placeholder' => 'Enter value',
        'maxlength' => 100
    ])

    // Form Type Options
    ->setFormTypeOption('attr.class', 'custom')       // Set single form type option
    ->setFormTypeOptions([                            // Set multiple form type options
        'attr' => ['class' => 'custom'],
        'required' => true
    ])

    // Custom Options
    ->setCustomOption('renderAsHtml', true)           // Set custom option
    ->setCustomOptions([                              // Set multiple custom options
        'renderAsHtml' => true,
        'hasOptions' => false
    ]);
```

### Resource Management
```php
$field
    // CSS Resources
    ->setCssResources([
        'custom/styles.css'
    ])
    ->appendCssResources(true)                   // Enable CSS resource appending

    // JavaScript Resources
    ->setJsResources([
        'custom/script.js'
    ])
    ->appendJsResources(true);                   // Enable JS resource appending
```

### Value Handling
```php
$field
    // Value Access
    ->getValue()                                 // Get current value
    ->getDefaultValue()                          // Get default value
    ->getProperty()                              // Get property name
    ->getDisplayPropertyPath()                   // Get display property path

    // Value Formatting
    ->setEscape(false)                          // Disable HTML escaping
    ->getFormattedValue($entity, $view)         // Get formatted value
    ->getFormattedLabel($view);                 // Get formatted label
```

### Unique Identification
```php
$field
    ->getUniqueId();                            // Get unique field identifier
```

### Common Options Reference

| Option | Method | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| Label | `setLabel()` | Field label displayed in forms and views |
| Property | `setProperty()` | Database field or property name |
| Input Type | `setInputType()` | HTML input type (text, number, etc.) |
| Required | `setRequired()` | Whether the field is required |
| Default Value | `setDefaultValue()` | Default value when creating new records |
| Help Text | `setHelp()` | Help text displayed below the field |
| CSS Class | `addCssClass()` | Additional CSS classes |
| Columns | `setColumns()` | Bootstrap grid column classes |
| Virtual | `setVirtual()` | Whether field exists in database |
| Sortable | `setSortable()` | Whether field can be sorted |
| Editable | `setEditable()` | Whether field can be edited |
| Escape | `setEscape()` | Whether to escape HTML in values |
| Custom Options | `setCustomOption()` | Custom field-specific options |
| Form Type Options | `setFormTypeOption()` | Form rendering options |
| Input Options | `setInputOption()` | HTML input attributes |
| Resources | `setCssResources()`, `setJsResources()` | Additional CSS/JS files |

### Display Pages

Fields can be configured to show/hide on specific pages:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Enum\Page;

$field
    ->showOn(Page::INDEX)      // Index/listing page
    ->showOn(Page::CSV)        // CSV export
    ->showOn(Page::ADD)        // Add/create form
    ->showOn(Page::EDIT)       // Edit form
    ->showOn(Page::VIEW)       // Detail view
    ->showOn(Page::BRIEF_VIEW) // Brief/summary view
    ->showOn(Page::INLINE_EDIT); // Inline editing
```

## Virtual Fields

Virtual fields can be implemented in two ways: through Entity accessors or using callback-based sorting.

### Entity Virtual Fields
Virtual fields defined in entities are great for display but cannot be used for sorting:

```php
// src/Model/Entity/User.php
class User extends Entity
{
    protected array $_virtual = ['full_name'];

    protected function _getFullName()
    {
        return $this->first_name . ' ' . $this->last_name;
    }
}

// In your Admin configuration
yield StringField::new('full_name')
    ->setLabel(__('Full Name'))
    ->setVirtual(true);
```

### Sortable Virtual Fields
For sortable virtual fields, use the `setVirtualCallback` method to define the sorting logic:

```php
yield StringField::new('full_name_sort')
    ->setLabel(__('Full Name'))
    ->setVirtual(true)
    ->setSortable(true)
    ->setVirtualCallback(function ($query) {
        return $query->func()->concat([
            'first_name' => 'identifier',
            ' ',
            'last_name' => 'identifier'
        ]);
    });
```

The callback receives the query object and should return an expression that defines how the field should be sorted.

### Complex Virtual Field Examples

#### Case-Insensitive Name Sorting
```php
yield StringField::new('full_name_sort')
    ->setLabel(__('Full Name'))
    ->setVirtual(true)
    ->setSortable(true)
    ->setVirtualCallback(function ($query) {
        return $query->func()->lower([
            $query->func()->concat([
                'first_name' => 'identifier',
                ' ',
                'last_name' => 'identifier'
            ])
        ]);
    });
```

#### Handling NULL Values
```php
yield StringField::new('full_name_sort')
    ->setLabel(__('Full Name'))
    ->setVirtual(true)
    ->setSortable(true)
    ->setVirtualCallback(function ($query) {
        return $query->func()->concat([
            $query->func()->coalesce([
                'first_name' => 'identifier',
                ''
            ]),
            ' ',
            $query->func()->coalesce([
                'last_name' => 'identifier',
                ''
            ])
        ]);
    });
```

#### Custom Status Order
```php
yield StringField::new('status_order')
    ->setLabel(__('Status'))
    ->setVirtual(true)
    ->setSortable(true)
    ->setVirtualCallback(function ($query) {
        return $query->newExpr(
            'CASE status
                WHEN "active" THEN 1
                WHEN "pending" THEN 2
                ELSE 3
            END'
        );
    });
```

### Key Points
- Entity virtual fields (`_get` methods) are good for display but cannot be sorted
- Use `setVirtualCallback` when you need sortable virtual fields
- The callback should return a valid database expression
- Virtual fields can combine multiple columns and include complex calculations

## Field Collections

Fields can be grouped into collections:

```php
$fields = FieldCollection::new([
    StringField::new('title'),
    TextField::new('content'),
    BoolField::new('published')
]);
```

## Form Initialization Interface

The `FormInitializationInterface` provides a standardized way for fields to perform custom initialization logic when forms are rendered, particularly useful for dependent/chained fields that need to pre-populate options based on existing entity data.

### Interface Methods

```php
interface FormInitializationInterface
{
    /**
     * Check if field needs form initialization
     *
     * @return bool True if field needs initialization
     */
    public function needsFormInitialization(): bool;

    /**
     * Initialize field data for form with entity data
     *
     * @param \Cake\Datasource\EntityInterface $entity Current entity being edited/viewed
     * @param string $page Current page context (edit/add/view)
     * @return void
     */
    public function initializeFormData(EntityInterface $entity, string $page): void;
}
```

### Usage Examples

#### Basic Implementation
```php
class CustomField extends BaseField implements FormInitializationInterface
{
    protected $onLoadCallback = null;

    public function setOnLoadCallback(callable $callback): self
    {
        $this->onLoadCallback = $callback;
        return $this;
    }

    public function needsFormInitialization(): bool
    {
        return $this->onLoadCallback !== null;
    }

    public function initializeFormData(EntityInterface $entity, string $page): void
    {
        if ($this->onLoadCallback) {
            $options = ($this->onLoadCallback)($entity, $this, $page);
            if (is_array($options)) {
                $this->setOptions($options);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

#### Field Configuration
```php
$field = CustomField::new('dependent_field')
    ->setOnLoadCallback(function($entity, $field, $page) {
        if ($page === 'edit' && $entity->get('parent_id')) {
            // Load dependent options based on parent value
            return $this->fetchTable('DependentModel')
                ->find('list')
                ->where(['parent_id' => $entity->get('parent_id')])
                ->toArray();
        }
        return [];
    });
```

### Benefits

- **Generic Interface**: Any field type can implement the interface
- **Page Context Awareness**: Callbacks receive page type (edit/add/view) for conditional logic
- **Entity Data Access**: Full access to current entity data for dynamic option loading
- **Error Handling**: Built-in error handling prevents form rendering failures
- **Performance**: Only fields that need initialization are processed

## Presentation Fields

Presentation fields provide specialized display elements without direct data binding.

### Link Button Field
Creates clickable buttons/links with icons and custom actions:

```php
yield LinkButtonField::new(
    (new EditLink())
        ->setLabel('Edit modal')
        ->setUrl(['action' => 'edit'])
        ->setAppendId(true)
        ->setModal(true)
        ->addCssClass('btn-info')
);
```
Important configuration options for link used by `LinkButtonField`:
- `setModal(true)`: Modal links are rendered as a modal dialog.
- `setAppendId(true)`: Appends the entity ID to the URL.

### Cell Field

Renders CakePHP cell content within the admin interface:

```php
yield CellField::new('UserStats')
    ->setAction('display')
    ->setOptions([
        'count' => 5
    ])
    ->setTemplate('compact')
    ->setDefaultColumns('col-md-6');
```

This field types are typically used for enhancing the display and interaction capabilities of your admin views rather than data input/editing.

## Layout Generation

The `LayoutGenerator` class handles automatic layout generation:

```php
$generator = new LayoutGenerator();
$fields = $generator->processFields($fields, 'edit');
```

### Tab Layout
```php
$fields = $generator->buildAsTabs([
    'details' => [
        'name' => 'Details',
        'content' => $detailsFields,
        'htmxOptions' => ['htmx' => false]
    ],
    'relations' => [
        'name' => 'Relations',
        'content' => $relationsFields,
        'htmxOptions' => [
            'htmx' => true,
            'url' => ['action' => 'relations']
        ]
    ]
]);
```

### Resources

Fields can include additional CSS/JS resources:

```php
$field
    ->setCssResources([
        'custom/styles.css'
    ])
    ->setJsResources([
        'custom/script.js'
    ]);
```

## Field Formatters

Field formatters control how field values are displayed in the admin interface. They transform raw data into formatted output suitable for display.

### Common Features

Fields can have multiple formatters that are applied in sequence. The BaseField class provides several methods to manage formatters:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\Field;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\Formatter\BoolFormatter;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\Formatter\EscapeFormatter;

// Add formatter at the end of chain
$field = Field::new('status')
    ->appendFormatter(new BoolFormatter());

// Add formatter at the beginning of chain
$field = Field::new('status')
    ->prependFormatter(new EscapeFormatter());

// Add formatter by class name
$field = Field::new('status')
    ->appendFormatter(PlainFormatter::class);

// Add formatter with options
$field = Field::new('status')
    ->appendFormatter('Url', [
        'url' => ['action' => 'view']
    ]);
```

### Formatter Chain

Formatters are applied in sequence, with each formatter receiving the output of the previous one:

```php
$field->getFormattedValue($entity, $view);  // Applies all formatters in chain
```

### Escaping Control

Fields provide built-in HTML escaping control:

```php
$field
    ->setEscape(false)  // Disable HTML escaping
    ->setEscape(true);  // Enable HTML escaping (default)
```

### Label Formatting

Fields can have separate formatters for their labels:

```php
$field->setLabelFormatter(new CustomLabelFormatter());
$field->getFormattedLabel($view);  // Get formatted label
```

### Integration Examples

#### Basic Field with Multiple Formatters

```php
$field = Field::new('price')
    ->appendFormatter(new EscapeFormatter())
    ->appendFormatter('Number', ['precision' => 2])
    ->appendFormatter(new CurrencyFormatter(['symbol' => '$']));
```

#### Field with Conditional Formatting

```php
if ($field->hasUrlFormatter()) {
    $field->appendFormatter(new UrlFormatter([
        'url' => ['controller' => 'Products', 'action' => 'view']
    ]));
}
```

#### Form Field with Label Formatting

```php
$field = Field::new('category_id')
    ->setLabelFormatter(new TranslateFormatter())
    ->appendFormatter(new SelectFormatter([
        'options' => $categories
    ]));
```

### Display Control

Fields can control where formatters are applied:

```php
$field->hideOnIndex();     // Don't show on index page
$field->onlyForms();       // Only show on forms
$field->hideOnView();      // Hide on view page
$field->showOn(Page::ADD); // Show only on add page
```

### Custom Options

Fields can pass custom options to formatters:

```php
$field
    ->setCustomOption(BaseField::OPTION_RENDER_AS_HTML, true)
    ->setCustomOption(BaseField::OPTION_HAS_OPTIONS, true)
    ->appendFormatter(new CustomFormatter());
```

## Built-in Formatters

### BoolFormatter
Formats boolean values as badges:
```php
$field->setFormatter(new BoolFormatter());
// Outputs: <span class="badge badge-pill badge-success">Yes</span>
//      or: <span class="badge badge-pill badge-danger">No</span>
```

### MultipleFormatter
Formats arrays or collections of related entities as badges:
```php
$field->setFormatter(
    (new MultipleFormatter())
        ->setBadgeClass('bg-primary')
);
// Outputs: <span class="badge bg-primary">Item 1</span> <span class="badge bg-primary">Item 2</span>
```

### UrlFormatter
Creates clickable links with configurable URLs:
```php
$field->setFormatter(
    (new UrlFormatter())
        ->setUrl(['controller' => 'Users', 'action' => 'view'])
        ->setUrlFieldParams(['id'])
);
```

### EscapeFormatter
Handles HTML escaping of field values:
```php
$field->setFormatter(new EscapeFormatter())
    ->setEscape(true);
```

### PlainFormatter
Displays raw field values with basic type handling:
```php
$field->setFormatter(new PlainFormatter());
```

### ZeroFormatter
Special handling for zero/null values:
```php
$field->setFormatter(new ZeroFormatter());
// Converts null to &nbsp;
```

### LegacyFormatter
Supports legacy formatting methods and helper callbacks:
```php
$field->setFormatter(new LegacyFormatter([
    'name' => 'Currency.format',
    'options' => ['USD']
]));
```

## Custom Formatters

Create custom formatters by extending BaseFormatter:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\Formatter\BaseFormatter;

class CustomFormatter extends BaseFormatter
{
    public function format(FieldInterface $field, EntityInterface $entity, View $view)
    {
        $value = $field->getValue();
        // Transform value
        return $transformedValue;
    }
}
```

## Formatter Configuration

Most formatters support additional configuration:

### URL Formatter Options
```php
$urlFormatter = new UrlFormatter();
$urlFormatter
    ->setUrl(['controller' => 'Posts', 'action' => 'view'])
    ->setUrlFieldParams(['id', 'slug'])
    ->setUrlOptions(['class' => 'btn btn-link'])
    ->setAssociationsLink(true);
```

### Multiple Formatter Options
```php
$multipleFormatter = new MultipleFormatter();
$multipleFormatter
    ->setBadgeClass('bg-info')  // Bootstrap badge class
```

### Legacy Formatter Options
```php
$legacyFormatter = new LegacyFormatter([
    'name' => 'Helper.method',
    'options' => ['option1', 'option2'],
    'callback' => function($entity, $value, $view) {
        return $view->Helper->customFormat($value);
    }
]);
```

## Helper Integration

Formatters can use view helpers for complex formatting:

```php
$field->setFormatter(new LegacyFormatter([
    'name' => 'Number.currency',
    'options' => ['USD', ['places' => 2]]
]));
```

## Label Formatters

Label formatters control how field labels are displayed in the admin interface. They provide a way to customize label rendering across different contexts.

### Basic Usage

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\Field;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\LabelFormatter\DefaultLabelFormatter;

$field = Field::new('user_id')
    ->setLabelFormatter(new DefaultLabelFormatter());
```

### Built-in Label Formatters

#### DefaultLabelFormatter
Returns the raw label value without modification:

```php
$field
    ->setLabel('User')
    ->setLabelFormatter(new DefaultLabelFormatter());
// Output: "User"
```

### Creating Custom Label Formatters

Create custom formatters by extending BaseLabelFormatter:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\LabelFormatter\BaseLabelFormatter;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\FieldInterface;
use Cake\View\View;

class TranslateLabelFormatter extends BaseLabelFormatter
{
    public function formatLabel(FieldInterface $field, View $view): string
    {
        return __($field->getLabel());
    }
}
```

#### Example Label Formatters

#### With Icon
```php
class IconLabelFormatter extends BaseLabelFormatter
{
    public function formatLabel(FieldInterface $field, View $view): string
    {
        $icon = $view->Html->tag('i', '', ['class' => 'fa fa-user']);
        return $icon . ' ' . $field->getLabel();
    }
}
```

#### With Required Indicator
```php
class RequiredLabelFormatter extends BaseLabelFormatter
{
    public function formatLabel(FieldInterface $field, View $view): string
    {
        $required = $field->isRequired() ? ' *' : '';
        return $field->getLabel() . $required;
    }
}
```
#### With Help Text
```php
class HelpLabelFormatter extends BaseLabelFormatter
{
    public function formatLabel(FieldInterface $field, View $view): string
    {
        $help = $field->getHelp();
        if ($help) {
            $helpIcon = $view->Html->tag('i', '', [
                'class' => 'fa fa-question-circle',
                'data-toggle' => 'tooltip',
                'title' => $help
            ]);
            return $field->getLabel() . ' ' . $helpIcon;
        }
        return $field->getLabel();
    }
}
```

### Using Label Formatters

#### Basic Field Configuration
```php
$field = Field::new('email')
    ->setLabel('Email Address')
    ->setLabelFormatter(new RequiredLabelFormatter());
```

#### Chaining with Other Field Settings
```php
$field = Field::new('status')
    ->setLabel('Account Status')
    ->setLabelFormatter(new IconLabelFormatter())
    ->setHelp('Current state of the account')
    ->appendFormatter(new BoolFormatter());
```

#### Dynamic Label Formatting
```php
$field->setLabelFormatter(new class extends BaseLabelFormatter {
    public function formatLabel(FieldInterface $field, View $view): string
    {
        return strtoupper($field->getLabel());
    }
});
```

### Integration with Views

Label formatters have access to the View object, allowing use of helpers and other view functionality:

```php
class BootstrapLabelFormatter extends BaseLabelFormatter
{
    public function formatLabel(FieldInterface $field, View $view): string
    {
        return $view->Html->tag('span', $field->getLabel(), [
            'class' => 'form-label'
        ]);
    }
}
```
## Field Extractors

Field extractors are responsible for retrieving values from entities for display in fields. They handle how data is pulled from your entities and prepared for formatting.

### Default Extractor

The `DefaultExtractor` is the standard extractor used when no custom extractor is specified. It handles common data extraction scenarios:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\Field;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\Extractor\DefaultExtractor;

$field = Field::new('user.profile.name')
    ->setExtractor(new DefaultExtractor());
```

#### Translation Extractor

TranslationExtractor is a special extractor that allows you to translate the value of a field. It prepares translations for a field and stores them in the field using `setTranslatedValues` method.



---

# AutocompleteField

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/Fields/Autocomplete.md

# AutocompleteField

The `AutocompleteField` provides a dynamic search field with server-side data retrieval, allowing users to search and select items from potentially large datasets without loading all options at once. It also supports local mode for smaller datasets and advanced customization options.

## Table of Contents
- [Basic Usage](#basic-usage)
- [Features](#features)
- [Configuration Options](#configuration-options)
  - [Essential Options](#essential-options)
  - [Performance Options](#performance-options)
  - [Dependent Fields Options](#dependent-fields-options)
  - [Display and Formatting Options](#display-and-formatting-options)
  - [Callback and Validation Options](#callback-and-validation-options)
  - [Local Mode Options](#local-mode-options)
- [Examples](#examples)
  - [Basic Autocomplete](#basic-autocomplete)
  - [Local Mode Autocomplete](#local-mode-autocomplete)
  - [Custom Display Format](#custom-display-format)
  - [Custom Suggestion Template](#custom-suggestion-template)
  - [Post-Select Callback](#post-select-callback)
  - [Empty State Handling](#empty-state-handling)
  - [Accessing Nested Properties](#accessing-nested-properties)
- [Cascading Autocomplete Fields](#cascading-autocomplete-fields)
  - [Simple Parent-Child Relationship](#simple-parent-child-relationship)
  - [Multi-Level Cascading with Ancestor Dependencies](#multi-level-cascading-with-ancestor-dependencies)
- [Custom Query Parameters](#custom-query-parameters)
- [Server-Side Implementation](#server-side-implementation)
  - [Autocomplete Processor](#autocomplete-processor)
  - [Custom Controller Action Implementation](#custom-controller-action-implementation)

## Basic Usage

```php
AutocompleteField::new('user_id')
    ->setLabel('User')
    ->setAutocompleteUrl('/admin/users/autocomplete')
    ->setIdName('id')
    ->setValueName('name');
```

## Features

- Asynchronous data loading with server-side filtering
- Local mode for small datasets (no server requests)
- Customizable search query parameters
- Dependent/chained autocomplete selects
- Debounced input for improved performance
- Keyboard navigation support
- Loading indicators during search
- Support for complex object paths
- Progressive loading of options
- Custom display formatting
- HTML suggestion templates
- Post-selection callbacks
- Validation callbacks
- Custom CSS classes
- Debug mode for troubleshooting

## Configuration Options

### Essential Options

| Method | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `setAutocompleteUrl()` | Set the URL for data fetching (array or string) | `null` |
| `setIdName()` | Set the property name for ID values in results | `'id'` |
| `setValueName()` | Set the property name for display values in results | `'name'` |
| `setQuery()` | Set the query string format for search | `'search=%QUERY'` |
| `setWildcard()` | Set the placeholder in query to be replaced by search term | `'%QUERY'` |

### Performance Options

| Method | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `setMinLength()` | Minimum characters before search triggers | `2` |
| `setDelay()` | Debounce delay in milliseconds | `300` |

### Dependent Fields Options

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `setParentField()` | Make this field dependent on another autocomplete field |
| `setAdditionalParents()` | Add ancestor dependencies (grandparent relationships) |
| `setCascadeEvent()` | Set custom event name for cascading updates |
| `setResetEvent()` | Set custom event name for resetting field |

### Display and Formatting Options

| Method | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `setDisplayFormat()` | Set custom format for input field display | `null` |
| `setSuggestionTemplate()` | Set HTML template for suggestion items | `null` |
| `setCustomClasses()` | Set CSS classes for suggestions and selected items | `null` |
| `setEmptyTemplate()` | Set a static HTML template for the empty (no results) state | `null` |
| `setEmptyCallback()` | Set a JS callback function name for dynamic empty rendering | `null` |

### Callback and Validation Options

| Method | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `setPostSelectCallback()` | Set JavaScript function to call after selection | `null` |
| `setValidationCallback()` | Set JavaScript function for validation | `null` |
| `setFormatCallback()` | Set JavaScript function for dynamic formatting | `null` |

### Local Mode Options

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `setOptions()` | Set local options array (enables local mode) |
| `setOptionsBuilder()` | Set callable to build options dynamically |
| `isLocalMode()` | Check if field is in local mode |
| `getLocalData()` | Get local data for autocomplete |

### Debug

| Method | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `setDebug()` | Enable debug logging | `false` |

## Examples

### Basic Autocomplete

```php
AutocompleteField::new('user_id')
    ->setLabel('User')
    ->setAutocompleteUrl(['controller' => 'Users', 'action' => 'autocomplete'])
    ->setIdName('id')
    ->setValueName('full_name')
    ->setQuery('search=%QUERY')
    ->setMinLength(2)
    ->setDelay(400);
```

### Local Mode Autocomplete

For smaller datasets, use local mode to avoid server requests:

```php
AutocompleteField::new('status')
    ->setLabel('Status')
    ->setOptions([
        'active' => 'Active',
        'inactive' => 'Inactive',
        'pending' => 'Pending',
        'completed' => 'Completed'
    ])
    ->setIdName('id')
    ->setValueName('name');
```

### Custom Display Format

Control how the selected value appears in the input field:

```php
AutocompleteField::new('user_id')
    ->setLabel('User')
    ->setAutocompleteUrl(['controller' => 'Users', 'action' => 'autocomplete'])
    ->setDisplayFormat('{title} {first_name} {last_name}')  // Shows "Dr. John Smith"
    ->setValueName('full_name_with_email');  // Used for searching
```

### Custom Suggestion Template

Create rich HTML suggestions with custom styling:

```php
AutocompleteField::new('user_id')
    ->setLabel('User')
    ->setAutocompleteUrl(['controller' => 'Users', 'action' => 'autocomplete'])
    ->setSuggestionTemplate('
        <div class="user-suggestion">
            <div class="name">{title} {first_name} {last_name}</div>
            <div class="email">{email}</div>
            <div class="department">{department}</div>
        </div>
    ')
    ->setCustomClasses('suggestion-item', 'selected-item');
```

### Post-Select Callback

Execute custom JavaScript after selection:

```php
AutocompleteField::new('user_id')
    ->setLabel('User')
    ->setAutocompleteUrl(['controller' => 'Users', 'action' => 'autocomplete'])
    ->setPostSelectCallback('App.handleUserSelection')
    ->setDebug(true);
```

JavaScript callback function:
```javascript
App.handleUserSelection = function(id, value, field, data) {
    console.log('Selected user:', { id, value, field, data });

    if (data && data.url) {
        window.location.href = data.url;
    }
};
```

### Empty State Handling

The `AutocompleteField` supports a customizable "empty" (no results) template and callback, allowing you to define what is shown when no results are found. This enables advanced use cases such as providing a link or button to add a new entity (e.g., "Add Item"), or displaying a context-aware message.

### Feature Summary
- Show a custom message or action when no autocomplete results are found
- Supports static HTML templates with placeholders (e.g., `{query}`, `{context.user_id}`)
- Supports dot notation for nested context properties in templates
- Supports dynamic rendering via a JavaScript callback

#### Placeholders for Templates
- `{query}`: The current search string
- `{parentId}`: (if applicable) The parent field value
- `{context.user_id}`: Access any value from the form context using dot notation
- `{parent.company_id}`: Access parent/ancestor field values using dot notation

#### Static Empty Template (with Dot Notation)
```php
AutocompleteField::new('user_id')
    ->setLabel('User')
    ->setAutocompleteUrl(['controller' => 'Users', 'action' => 'autocomplete'])
    ->setEmptyTemplate('<div class="autocomplete-empty">No user found for "{query}". <a href="/admin/users/add?name={query}">Add new user</a></div>');
```

#### Dynamic JavaScript Callback
```php
AutocompleteField::new('user_id')
    ->setLabel('User')
    ->setAutocompleteUrl(['controller' => 'Users', 'action' => 'autocomplete'])
    ->setEmptyCallback('renderEmptyUser');
```

**JavaScript callback example:**
```js
function renderEmptyUser(query, ctx) {
    // ctx contains additional info (field, parent, context, etc.)
    return `<div class="autocomplete-empty">No user found for "${query}". <button onclick=\"openAddUserModal('${query}')\">Add User</button></div>`;
}

function openAddUserModal(name) {
    // Your modal logic here
    alert('Open modal to add: ' + name);
}
```

#### Form Context & Dot Notation
The autocomplete system builds a **form context** object, including:
- The current field name
- The current search query
- All parent/ancestor field values (for cascaded autocompletes, under `parent`)
- **All form field values** (using vanilla JS form serialization, under `context`)

You can use dot notation in your empty template placeholders to access nested properties of the context object. This allows you to reference any value in the context, including all form fields and parent/ancestor fields.

**Examples:**
- `{context.user_id}` → value of `user_id` from the form
- `{parent.company_id}` → value of `company_id` from parent fields
- `{query}` → the current search string

When rendering the template, the system will resolve dot notation to the correct value in the context object.


### Accessing Nested Properties

Access values from nested objects:

```php
AutocompleteField::new('article_id')
    ->setLabel('Article')
    ->setAutocompleteUrl(['controller' => 'Articles', 'action' => 'autocomplete'])
    ->setIdName('id')
    ->setValueName('title')  // Simple property
    // OR
    ->setValueName('author.name');  // Nested property path
```

## Cascading Autocomplete Fields

### Simple Parent-Child Relationship

Autocomplete fields can be chained together to create dependent selects, where the child field's options depend on the selected value in the parent field. When a parent field's value changes, all dependent child fields are reset and disabled until a new parent value is selected.

```php
// Parent field
$countryField = AutocompleteField::new('country_id')
    ->setLabel('Country')
    ->setAutocompleteUrl('/admin/countries/autocomplete');

// Child field depends on parent
$cityField = AutocompleteField::new('city_id')
    ->setLabel('City')
    ->setAutocompleteUrl('/admin/cities/autocomplete')
    ->setParentField($countryField, 'country_id');
```

When the user selects a country, the `country_id` parameter is automatically added to the city autocomplete URL, filtering the available cities.

### Multi-Level Cascading with Ancestor Dependencies

For more complex hierarchies with three or more levels, you'll need to use `setParentField()` for the direct parent and `setAdditionalParents()` to maintain the grandparent (or higher ancestor) relationship:

```php
// Level 1 - Top parent
$regionField = AutocompleteField::new('region_id')
    ->setLabel('Region')
    ->setAutocompleteUrl('/admin/regions/autocomplete');

// Level 2 - Child of region, parent of employee
$departmentField = AutocompleteField::new('department_id')
    ->setLabel('Department')
    ->setParentField($regionField, 'region_id')  // Direct parent relationship
    ->setAutocompleteUrl('/admin/departments/autocomplete');

// Level 3 - Child of department, grandchild of region
$employeeField = AutocompleteField::new('employee_id')
    ->setLabel('Employee')
    ->setAutocompleteUrl('/admin/employees/autocomplete')
    ->setParentField($departmentField, 'department_id')  // Direct parent relationship
    ->setAdditionalParents([
        ['field' => $regionField, 'param' => 'region_id']  // Grandparent relationship
    ]);
```

In this example:
1. Selecting a region will reset and filter departments
2. Selecting a department will reset and filter employees
3. When querying for employees, both the department_id and region_id parameters are sent
4. If the region changes, both department and employee fields will be reset

This ensures that employees are filtered not just by their department but also by the higher-level region, maintaining consistency in multi-level hierarchies.

## Custom Query Parameters

Customize how search parameters are sent to the server:

```php
AutocompleteField::new('product_id')
    ->setLabel('Product')
    ->setAutocompleteUrl('/admin/products/search')
    ->setQuery('term=%QUERY&type=active')
    ->setWildcard('%QUERY');
```

## Server-Side Implementation

### Autocomplete Processor

The Admin plugin includes an autocomplete processor that simplifies serving data to autocomplete fields.

### Custom Controller Action Implementation

Create a controller action to handle autocomplete requests:

```php
// In ProductsController.php
public function autocomplete()
{
    $this->viewBuilder()->setClassName('Json');
    $term = $this->request->getQuery('search');

    $products = $this->Products->find()
        ->select(['id', 'name', 'price'])
        ->where(['name LIKE' => "%$term%"])
        ->limit(10)
        ->all();

    $list = $products->map(function ($product) {
        return [
            'id' => $product->id,
            'name' => $product->name,
            'price' => $product->price
        ];
    });

    return $this->getResponse()->withStringBody(json_encode(['list' => $list]));
}
```

# Builder

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/Fields/Builder.md

# Builder

## Table of Contents
- [Overview](#overview)
- [Basic Configuration](#basic-configuration)
- [Block Types](#block-types)
- [Field Configuration](#field-configuration)
- [Formatters](#formatters)
- [Validation](#validation)
- [Layout Patterns](#layout-patterns)
- [Examples](#examples)

## Overview

The Builder field provides a flexible way to create dynamic content blocks with different types, fields, and formatting options. It's particularly useful for:

- Page builders
- Dynamic content management (CMS)
- Flexible form layouts
- Custom block-based interfaces

## Basic Configuration

### Setting Up a Builder

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\BuilderField;

class PagesSettings extends SettingsExt
{
    public function fieldsBuilder(string $page): iterable
    {
        yield BuilderField::new('content', 'Page Content')
            ->hideOnIndex()
            ->setUnlocked(true);
    }
}
```

## Block Types

### Adding Blocks

```php
$builder->addBlock('header', 'Header Block', function ($block) {
    $block
        ->addField(
            TextField::new('title', 'Title')
                ->setRequired(true)
        )
        ->addField(
            SelectField::new('level', 'Heading Level')
                ->setOptions([
                    'h1' => 'H1',
                    'h2' => 'H2',
                ])
        )
        ->setFormatter(new HeaderBlockFormatter());
});
```

### Block Features
- Multiple field types per block
- Custom validation rules
- Block-specific formatters
- Reordering capabilities
- Copy/paste functionality
- Nested collections

## Formatters

### Creating Block Formatters

```php
class HeaderBlockFormatter implements FormatterInterface
{
    public function format(FieldInterface $field, EntityInterface $data, View $view): string
    {
        $level = $data['level'] ?? 'h2';
        $title = $data['title'] ?? '';

        return sprintf(
            '<%1$s class="block-header">%2$s</%1$s>',
            h($level),
            h($title)
        );
    }
}
```

## Layout Patterns

### Container Patterns

```php
$builder->setContainerPattern(function() {
    yield FormField::addRow();
    yield BuilderPlaceholderField::new();
});
```

## Complete Example

```php
yield BuilderField::new('data', 'Page Content')
    ->hideOnIndex()
    ->addBlock('text', 'Text Block', function ($block) {
        $block
            ->addField(
                CollectionField::new('tags', 'Tags')
                    ->setAllowAdd(true)
                    ->setAllowDelete(true)
                    ->setMax(5)
                    ->addNestedField(
                        StringField::new('tag', 'Tag')
                    )
            )
            ->addField(
                TextField::new('content', 'Content')
                    ->setRequired(true)
                    ->addValidationRule('notEmptyString', 'Content required')
            )
            ->setFormatter(new TextBlockFormatter());
    })
    ->setContainerPattern(function() {
        yield FormField::addRow();
        yield BuilderPlaceholderField::new();
    });
```

## Available Actions

The builder supports several built-in actions:

- `ACTION_ADD_BLOCK`: Add a new block
- `ACTION_REMOVE_BLOCK`: Remove existing block
- `ACTION_MOVE_UP`: Move block up
- `ACTION_MOVE_DOWN`: Move block down
- `ACTION_COPY_BLOCK`: Duplicate block
- `ACTION_REORDER`: Reorder blocks via drag and drop

## HTMX Integration

The builder uses HTMX for dynamic interactions:

```html
<button type="button"
    hx-post=""
    hx-target="closest form"
    hx-swap="outerHTML"
    hx-headers='{"X-Builder-Action": "add_block", "X-Builder-Field": "content"}'>
    Add Block
</button>
```

## Validation

### Block-Level Validation

```php
$block->addField(
    TextField::new('title')
        ->setRequired(true)
        ->addValidationRule('notEmptyString', 'Title required')
        ->addValidationRule(['maxLength', 255], 'Title too long')
);
```

### Builder-Level Validation

```php
$builder->addValidationRule('validBlockTypes', [
    'rule' => function ($value) {
        if (!is_array($value)) {
            return false;
        }
        foreach ($value as $block) {
            if (!isset($block['type'])) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    },
    'message' => 'Invalid block structure'
]);
```

## Examples

### Content Builder

```php
yield BuilderField::new('data', 'Page Content')
    ->hideOnIndex()
    ->addBlock('header', 'Header Block', function ($block) {
        $block
            ->addField(
                TextField::new('title', 'Title')
                    ->setRequired(true)
                    ->addValidationRule('notEmptyString', 'Title required')
                    ->addValidationRule(['maxLength', 255], 'Title too long')
            )
            ->addField(
                SelectField::new('level', 'Heading Level')
                    ->setOptions([
                        'h1' => 'H1',
                        'h2' => 'H2',
                        'h3' => 'H3',
                    ])
                    ->setValue('h2')
            )
            ->addField(
                TextField::new('subtitle', 'Subtitle')
            )
            ->setFormatter(new HeaderBlockFormatter());
    })
    ->addBlock('text', 'Text Block', function ($block) {
        $block
            ->addField(
                CollectionField::new('tags', 'Tags')
                    ->setAllowAdd(true)
                    ->setAllowDelete(true)
                    ->setMax(5)
                    ->addNestedField(
                        StringField::new('tag', 'Tag')
                    )
            )
            ->addField(
                TextField::new('content', 'Content')
                    ->setRequired(true)
            )
            ->setFormatter(new TextBlockFormatter());
    })
    ->addBlock('image', 'Image Block', function ($block) {
        $block
            ->addField(
                TextField::new('caption', 'Caption')
                    ->setRequired(true)
            )
            ->addField(
                SelectField::new('size', 'Image Size')
                    ->setOptions([
                        'small' => 'Small (300px)',
                        'medium' => 'Medium (600px)',
                        'large' => 'Large (900px)',
                    ])
                    ->setValue('medium')
            )
            ->setFormatter(new ImageBlockFormatter());
    });
```

### Custom Block Formatter

```php
class TextBlockFormatter implements FormatterInterface
{
    public function format(FieldInterface $field, EntityInterface $data, View $view): string
    {
        $content = $data['content'] ?? '';
        $tags = $data['tags'] ?? [];

        $tagsHtml = '';
        if (!empty($tags)) {
            $tagsHtml = '<div class="block-tags">';
            foreach ($tags as $tag) {
                $tagsHtml .= sprintf(
                    '<span class="tag">%s</span>',
                    h($tag['tag'])
                );
            }
            $tagsHtml .= '</div>';
        }

        return sprintf(
            '<div class="block-text">%s%s</div>',
            $tagsHtml,
            nl2br(h($content))
        );
    }
}
```

### Block with Nested Collections

```php
->addBlock('gallery', 'Gallery Block', function ($block) {
    $block
        ->addField(
            TextField::new('title', 'Gallery Title')
        )
        ->addField(
            CollectionField::new('images', 'Images')
                ->setAllowAdd(true)
                ->setAllowDelete(true)
                ->setMax(12)
                ->addNestedField(
                    StringField::new('url', 'Image URL')
                )
                ->addNestedField(
                    TextField::new('caption', 'Caption')
                )
                ->addNestedField(
                    SelectField::new('size', 'Size')
                        ->setOptions([
                            'small' => 'Small',
                            'medium' => 'Medium',
                            'large' => 'Large',
                        ])
                )
        )
        ->setFormatter(new GalleryBlockFormatter());
});
```

# Creating a Custom Field in CakePHP: Color Picker Implementation

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/Fields/CustomField.md

# Creating a Custom Field in CakePHP: Color Picker Implementation

Here is a complete guide of creating a custom field for the CakePHP Admin plugin.

## 1. Create the Field Class

First, create the ColorPickerField class that defines the field's behavior and configuration:

```php:src/Settings/Field/ColorPickerField.php
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Settings\Field;

use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\BaseField;

class ColorPickerField extends BaseField
{
    public static function new(string $propertyName, ?string $label = null): self
    {
        $field = new self();
        $field
            ->setProperty($propertyName)
            ->setInputType('colorpicker')
            ->setLabel($label)
            ->addCssClass('field-colorpicker')
            ->setDefaultColumns('col-md-6 col-xxl-5')
            ->setCustomOption(self::OPTION_RENDER_AS_HTML, false)
            ->setCustomOption(self::OPTION_HAS_OPTIONS, false)
            ->setFormTypeOptions([
                'format' => 'hex',
                'alpha' => true,
                'swatches' => [],
                'theme' => 'default',
                'themeMode' => 'light',
                'clearButton' => false,
                'closeButton' => true,
            ])
            ->setJsResources([
                'coloris.min.js',
                'form/colorpicker.js',
            ])
            ->setCssResources([
                'coloris.min.css',
            ]);

        return $field;
    }

    public function setFormat(string $format): self
    {
        $this->setFormTypeOption('format', $format);
        return $this;
    }

    public function setAlpha(bool $enabled): self
    {
        $this->setFormTypeOption('alpha', $enabled);
        return $this;
    }

    public function setSwatches(array $swatches): self
    {
        $this->setFormTypeOption('swatches', $swatches);
        return $this;
    }

    public function setTheme(string $theme): self
    {
        $this->setFormTypeOption('theme', $theme);
        return $this;
    }

    public function setThemeMode(string $mode): self
    {
        $this->setFormTypeOption('themeMode', $mode);
        return $this;
    }

    public function setClearButton(bool $enabled): self
    {
        $this->setFormTypeOption('clearButton', $enabled);
        return $this;
    }

    public function setCloseButton(bool $enabled): self
    {
        $this->setFormTypeOption('closeButton', $enabled);
        return $this;
    }
}
```

## 2. Create the Field Trait

Create ColorPickerTrait to handle the field's rendering logic:

```php:src/View/Helper/Form/ColorPickerTrait.php
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\View\Helper\Form;

trait ColorPickerTrait
{
    public function initializeColorPicker(): void
    {
        $this->setTemplates([
            'colorpickerContainer' => '<div class="colorpicker-wrapper{{containerClass}}"{{containerAttrs}}>{{content}}</div>',
            'colorpickerInputWrapper' => '<div class="input-wrapper">{{input}}{{error}}</div>',
        ]);
    }

    public function colorPickerControl(string $fieldName, array $options = []): string
    {
        $options['type'] = 'text';
        $options['class'] = ($options['class'] ?? '') . ' colorpicker-input';
        $options['data-coloris'] = '';
        $containerOptions = $options['container'] ?? [];
        unset($options['container']);

        $dataAttributes = [
            'format',
            'alpha',
            'swatches',
            'theme',
            'themeMode',
            'clearButton',
            'closeButton',
        ];

        foreach ($dataAttributes as $attr) {
            if (isset($options[$attr])) {
                $key = 'data-' . strtolower(preg_replace('/([A-Z])/', '-$1', $attr));
                $options[$key] = is_array($options[$attr])
                    ? json_encode($options[$attr])
                    : $options[$attr];
                unset($options[$attr]);
            }
        }

        $input = parent::control($fieldName, $options);

        $inputWrapper = $this->formatTemplate('colorpickerInputWrapper', [
            'input' => $input,
            'error' => '',
        ]);

        $containerClass = '';
        $containerAttrs = '';

        if (isset($containerOptions['class'])) {
            $containerClass = ' ' . $containerOptions['class'];
            unset($containerOptions['class']);
        }
        if (!empty($containerOptions)) {
            $containerAttrs = $this->templater()->formatAttributes($containerOptions);
        }

        return $this->formatTemplate('colorpickerContainer', [
            'content' => $inputWrapper,
            'containerClass' => $containerClass,
            'containerAttrs' => $containerAttrs
        ]);
    }
}
```

## 3. Create Custom Form Helper

Override the default Form Helper:

```php:src/View/Helper/BootstrapUIFormHelper.php
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\View\Helper;

use App\View\Helper\Form\ColorPickerTrait;
use CakeDC\Admin\View\Helper\BootstrapUIFormHelper as FormHelper;

class BootstrapUIFormHelper extends FormHelper
{
    use ColorPickerTrait;

    protected function initializeControls(): void
    {
        parent::initializeControls();
        $this->initializeColorPicker();
    }

    public function handleControlType(string $fieldName, array $options): string
    {
        if (!isset($options['type'])) {
            return parent::handleControlType($fieldName, $options);
        }

        if ($options['type'] === 'colorpicker') {
            unset($options['type']);
            return $this->colorpickerControl($fieldName, $options);
        }

        return parent::handleControlType($fieldName, $options);
    }
}
```

## 4. Update ControlTypeTrait

Add the ColorPickerTrait to the main ControlTypeTrait:

```php:src/View/Helper/Form/ControlTypeTrait.php
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\View\Helper\Form;

trait ControlTypeTrait
{
    use ColorPickerTrait;
    // ... other traits ...

    protected function initializeControls(): void
    {
        $this->initializeColorPicker();
        // ... other initializations ...
    }

    public function handleControlType(string $fieldName, array $options): string
    {
        if (!isset($options['type'])) {
            return parent::control($fieldName, $options);
        }

        if ($options['type'] === 'colorpicker') {
            unset($options['type']);
            return $this->colorpickerControl($fieldName, $options);
        }

        // ... other handlers ...
        return parent::control($fieldName, $options);
    }
}
```

## 5. Create JavaScript Handler

Create the JavaScript file for client-side functionality:

```javascript:webroot/js/form/colorpicker.js
if (!window.AdminFields?.ColorPickerField) {
    class ColorPickerField {
        static selector = '.colorpicker-wrapper:not([data-initialized])';

        static init(element) {
            const wrappers = element.querySelectorAll(this.selector);
            wrappers.forEach(wrapper => {
                const input = wrapper.querySelector('.colorpicker-input');
                if (!input) return;

                const options = {
                    format: this.getDataAttribute(input, 'format', 'hex'),
                    alpha: this.getDataAttribute(input, 'alpha', true),
                    theme: this.getDataAttribute(input, 'theme', 'default'),
                    themeMode: this.getDataAttribute(input, 'theme-mode', 'light'),
                    clearButton: this.getDataAttribute(input, 'clear-button', false),
                    closeButton: this.getDataAttribute(input, 'close-button', true),
                };

                const swatches = this.getDataAttribute(input, 'swatches', []);
                if (swatches.length) {
                    options.swatches = typeof swatches === 'string'
                        ? JSON.parse(swatches)
                        : swatches;
                }

                Coloris.setInstance(`#${input.id}`, options);
                wrapper.dataset.initialized = 'true';
            });
        }

        static getDataAttribute(element, name, defaultValue) {
            const value = element.getAttribute(`data-${name}`);
            if (value === null) return defaultValue;
            if (value === 'true') return true;
            if (value === 'false') return false;
            return value;
        }
    }

    window.AdminFields = window.AdminFields || {};
    window.AdminFields.ColorPickerField = ColorPickerField;
}
```

## 6. Configure Asset Loading

Register the field in your bootstrap configuration:

```php:config/bootstrap_after.php
<?php
use Cake\Core\Configure;

Configure::write('Admin.assets.fields', [
    \App\Settings\Field\ColorPickerField::class,
]);
```

## Usage

After setting up all components, you can use the ColorPicker field like this:

```php
use App\Settings\Field\ColorPickerField;

ColorPickerField::new('color', 'Choose Color')
    ->setFormat('rgb')
    ->setAlpha(true)
    ->setTheme('default')
    ->setThemeMode('light');
```

## Key Implementation Details

1. **Field Configuration**: The ColorPickerField class provides a fluent interface for configuring all aspects of the color picker, including format, alpha channel, swatches, theme, and buttons.

2. **Data Flow**: Options set in PHP are passed to JavaScript through data attributes, which are processed by the ColorPickerTrait.

3. **Template Structure**: The field uses nested templates (colorpickerContainer and colorpickerInputWrapper) for flexible rendering.

4. **JavaScript Integration**: The ColorPickerField JavaScript class automatically initializes the Coloris color picker library with the configured options.

5. **Asset Management**: Required JavaScript and CSS files are automatically included through the field's configuration.

This implementation provides a complete, reusable color picker field that integrates seamlessly with CakePHP's form system while maintaining flexibility for customization.

---

# File Fields

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/Fields/FileField.md

# File Fields

File fields are used to upload files and images.

## File Storage Plugin

File fields use the [File Storage Plugin](https://github.com/CakeDC/cakephp-file-storage.git) to handle the file upload and storage.

It should be installed and configured before using file fields.

## File Field

The File Field is a field that allows you to upload a file. It automatically handles the file upload and storage, and provides a way to display the file. Also it handles automatic old file replacement when the field is edited.

### File Configuration
- `setAccept()`: Set allowed file types (e.g., '.pdf,.doc', 'image/*')
- `setAdapter()`: Set storage adapter ('Local', 'S3', etc.)
- `setAssociation()`: Set the related table association name

### Model association

```php
        $this->hasOne('Attachments', [
            'className' => 'Burzum/FileStorage.FileStorage',
            'foreignKey' => 'foreign_key',
            'conditions' => [
                'Attachments.model' => 'Attachments',
            ],
        ]);
```

### Entity configuration

```php

    protected array $_accessible = [
        'attachment' => true,
    ];


```

### Settings

In the SettingsExt, you can use the FileField to upload a file. Accessor `setAssociation` is used to set the association name defined in the model.

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\FileField;

    yield FileField::new('attachment')
        ->setAssociation('Attachments')
        ->setLabel('Attachment');
```

## Image Field

The Image Field is a field that allows you to upload an image. It automatically handles the image upload and storage, and provides a way to display the image. Also it handles automatic old image replacement when the field is edited.

### Image Configuration
- `setAccept()`: Set allowed file types (e.g., '.pdf,.doc', 'image/*')
- `setAdapter()`: Set storage adapter ('Local', 'S3', etc.)
- `setAssociation()`: Set the related table association name
- `setDimensions()`: Set image width and height constraints
- `setOptions()`: Set HTML options for image display

### Model association

```php
    $this->hasOne('Images', [
        'className' => 'Burzum/FileStorage.FileStorage',
        'foreignKey' => 'foreign_key',
        'conditions' => [
            'Images.model' => 'Images',
        ],
    ]);
```

### Entity configuration

```php
    protected array $_accessible = [
        'image' => true,
    ];
```

### Settings

In the SettingsExt, you can use the ImageField to upload an image. Accessor `setAssociation` is used to set the association name defined in the model.

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\ImageFileField;

    yield ImageFileField::new('image')
        ->setAssociation('Images')
        ->setLabel('Image');
```

The field automatically handles:
- Image upload and storage
- Old image cleanup on update
- File type validation
- Association management
- Dimension constraints
- HTML display options
