# Reports

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/Reports/Index.md

# Reports

## Table of Contents
- [Overview](#overview)
- [User Experience](#user-experience)
- [Report Types](#report-types)
- [Report Action](#report-action)
- [Report Registration with SettingsExt](#report-registration-with-settingsext)
- [Common Report Features](#common-report-features)
  - [Dynamic Content](#dynamic-content)
  - [Custom Query Building](#custom-query-building)
  - [Custom Styles](#custom-styles)
- [Report Engines](#report-engines)
- [Report Processing](#report-processing)
- [Report Registration](#report-registration)
- [Report Helpers](#report-helpers)
- [Additional Topics](#additional-topics)

## Overview

The Reports system provides a flexible framework for generating and rendering data reports in various formats. It supports different report types from simple tabular data to complex hierarchical grouping with aggregation.

Key features:
- Multiple report types (Table, Row Group, Composed Row, Pivot)
- Multiple output formats (HTML, PDF, Excel)
- Extensible engine system
- Field-based configuration
- Grouping and calculation capabilities
- Streaming data processing for large datasets
- Custom template support
- Dynamic content generation
- Custom query building
- Consistent rendering through helper classes

## User Experience

The Reports system includes interactive features that allow users to save and manage their report configurations:

### Saved Reports

Users can save their report configurations including all filter settings:

#### Managing Saved Reports
1. After applying filters to a report, users can save the current configuration:
   - Click the "Save" button in the saved reports panel
   - Enter a name for the report configuration
   - Optionally set additional options:
     - Add to favorites for quick access
     - Make public to share with other users
     - Set color and icon for visual identification

#### Accessing Saved Reports
The saved reports panel displays available reports organized by category:
- Favorites: Reports marked as favorites for quick access
- User Reports: Personal reports created by the current user
- Public Reports: Reports shared by other users

#### Switching Between Reports
1. Click on any saved report name to apply its configuration
2. The report will immediately update with the saved filter settings

#### Editing and Deleting Reports
1. For each saved report, users can:
   - Edit: Modify the report's name, icon, color, or sharing settings
   - Delete: Remove the saved report configuration

Saved reports are automatically stored on the server and will be available across sessions.

## Report Types

The admin system includes several report types to handle different data presentation needs:

### Table Reports

[Table Reports](TableReports.md) provide a simple tabular view of data without grouping. They're useful for straightforward data presentation where you need to display data in a list format without hierarchical organization.

### Group Reports

[Group Reports](GroupReports.md) organize data in hierarchical groups with support for aggregations and calculations. This includes:

- **Row Group Reports**: Standard grouped reports with headers and footers
- **Composed Row Reports**: Treat groups as complete units with detailed formatting

### Pivot Reports

[Pivot Reports](Pivot.md) organize data in a cross-tabular format (rows and columns) with aggregations at intersections. They're ideal for:

- Summarizing large datasets
- Showing data trends across different dimensions
- Creating matrix-style reports with dynamic columns
- Displaying totals and subtotals

## Report Action

The `ReportAction` class integrates reports into the admin interface:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\ReportAction;
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\Engine\PdfEngine;
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\Engine\ExcelEngine;
use App\Report\SalesReport;

// Create report action
$reportAction = new ReportAction();
$reportAction
    ->setName('sales_report')
    ->setLabel('Sales Report')
    ->setReport(new SalesReport());

// Configure available engines
$reportAction->enableEngine('pdf', PdfEngine::class, [
    'download' => true,
]);

$reportAction->enableEngine('excel', ExcelEngine::class);

// Disable an engine if needed
$reportAction->disableEngine('html');

// Add to actions list
$this->getActionsList()->add($reportAction);
```

### Engine Management

The `ReportAction` class provides methods for managing report engines:

```php
// Enable an engine
$reportAction->enableEngine('name', EngineClass::class, $config);

// Disable an engine
$reportAction->disableEngine('name');

// Check if an engine is enabled
$isEnabled = $reportAction->isEngineEnabled('name');

// Get all enabled engines
$engines = $reportAction->getEnabledEngines();

// Get an engine instance
$engine = $reportAction->getEngine('name');

// Get the appropriate engine for a format
$engine = $reportAction->getEngineForFormat('pdf');
```

## Report Registration with SettingsExt

Based on the code example you provided, here's a detailed explanation of how the Report Registration system works:

### Using Constants for Report Identifiers

For better code organization and maintainability, you should define constants for report identifiers:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\SettingsExt;
use App\Report\HoursReport;

class TimeSettings extends SettingsExt
{
    // Define constants for report identifiers
    const HOURS_REPORT = 'hoursReport';

    /**
     * @inheritDoc
     */
    public function loadDefaultActions(): void
    {
        parent::loadDefaultActions();

        // Register report using the constant identifier
        $this->addReport(new HoursReport(), self::HOURS_REPORT);
    }
}
```

Using constants for report identifiers:
- Ensures consistency when referencing reports in multiple places
- Prevents typos in string identifiers
- Makes it easier to refactor report names later
- Provides better IDE auto-completion support

#### Template Overloading for Reports

When registering reports with `addReport()`, you can customize the templates used for rendering by providing template options:

```php
$this->addReport(new SalesReport(), 'sales_report', [
    'templatePlugin' => 'MyPlugin',
    'templatePath' => 'Admin/CustomReports',
]);
```

#### Template Configuration Options

The `addReport()` method accepts the following template-related options:

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `templatePlugin` | The plugin containing report templates | 'CakeDC/Admin' |
| `templatePath` | The path to report templates within the plugin | 'Admin/Reports' |


### Integrating with the Search System

Reports can provide their own search functionality by implementing the `searchBuilder` method. The `SettingsExt` class integrates this with the admin's search system:

```php
use Cake\Http\ServerRequest;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\ReportAction;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Search\BaseSearch;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Search\DefaultSearch;

class TimeSettings extends SettingsExt
{
    /**
     * @inheritDoc
     */
    public function searchBuilder(string $page, ServerRequest $request): ?BaseSearch
    {
        // Get the current action
        $action = $this->getCurrentAction();

        // If the action is a report, use its search builder
        if ($action instanceof ReportAction) {
            return $action->getReport()->searchBuilder($request);
        }

        // For non-report actions, use the default search
        $engine = new DefaultSearch();
        // Configure default search...

        return $engine;
    }
}
```

This integration:
1. Detects when a report page is being viewed
2. Delegates to the report's `searchBuilder` method for custom search functionality
3. Falls back to default search for non-report pages

### Implementing Report-Specific Search

Each report can define its own search fields and behavior by implementing the `searchBuilder` method:

```php
use Cake\Http\ServerRequest;
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\BaseReport;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Search\BaseSearch;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Search\DefaultSearch;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\DateField;

class HoursReport extends BaseReport
{
    public function searchBuilder(ServerRequest $request): ?BaseSearch
    {
        $search = new DefaultSearch();

        // Add date range fields
        $search->addField(
            SearchField::new('date_from', 'Input')
                ->setPlaceholder('From Date')
        );

        $search->addField(
            SearchField::new('date_to', 'Input')
                ->setPlaceholder('To Date')
        );

        return $search;
    }
}
```

This allows each report to have its own specific search form with fields relevant to that report.

### Workflow

When implementing reports with search functionality:

1. Create your report class extending `BaseReport` (or a subclass like `TableReport` or `RowGroupReport`)
2. Implement the `searchBuilder` method to define search fields
3. Register the report in your settings class using `addReport()`
4. Override the `searchBuilder` method in your settings class to delegate to the report's search builder
5. The report's search functionality will be automatically integrated with the admin interface

## Common Report Features

All report types extend from `BaseReport` and share common functionality for configuration, data processing, and rendering.

### Dynamic Content

Reports support dynamic content through closures for titles and descriptions:

```php
use Cake\Http\ServerRequest;

// Dynamic title based on request parameters
$report->setTitle(function (ServerRequest $request): string {
    return 'Sales Report: ' . $request->getQuery('date_range');
});

// Dynamic description based on request parameters
$report->setDescription(function (ServerRequest $request): string {
    $region = $request->getQuery('region', 'All Regions');
    $product = $request->getQuery('product', 'All Products');
    return "Sales data for {$region}, {$product}";
});
```

The closures receive the current request object, allowing for context-aware report titles and descriptions that can change based on filtering parameters.

### Custom Query Building

Reports can customize how their data query is built using a query builder callback:

```php
use Cake\ORM\Query\SelectQuery;

$report->setQueryBuilder(function (SelectQuery $query, array $params): SelectQuery {
    // Apply base filters
    $query->where(['is_active' => true]);

    // Apply dynamic filters from request
    if (!empty($params['category_id'])) {
        $query->where(['category_id' => $params['category_id']]);
    }

    if (!empty($params['date_from'])) {
        $query->where(['created >=' => $params['date_from']]);
    }

    if (!empty($params['date_to'])) {
        $query->where(['created <=' => $params['date_to']]);
    }

    // Apply default sorting
    $query->orderBy(['name' => 'ASC']);

    return $query;
});
```

This allows for dynamic query construction based on user input and custom business logic.

### Custom Styles

Reports can use different templates for different output engines:

```php
// Set style for a specific engine
$report->setReportStyle('html', 'CakeDC/Admin.report/table');
$report->setReportStyle('pdf', 'CakeDC/Admin.report/pdf/table');
$report->setReportStyle('excel', 'CakeDC/Admin.report/excel/table');

// Set all styles at once
$report->setReportStyles([
    'html' => 'CakeDC/Admin.report/table',
    'pdf' => 'CakeDC/Admin.report/pdf/table',
    'excel' => 'CakeDC/Admin.report/excel/table',
]);
```

Each engine can have its own template, allowing for optimized rendering for each output format.

## Report Engines

The Reports system supports multiple output formats through a pluggable engine architecture. Each engine handles a specific output format.

### HTML Engine

The HTML engine is the default engine for rendering reports in web browsers:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\Engine\HtmlEngine;

// HTML engine is enabled by default
$reportAction->enableEngine('html', HtmlEngine::class, [
    // Optional configuration
]);
```

### PDF Engine

The PDF engine renders reports as downloadable PDF documents:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\Engine\PdfEngine;

$reportAction->enableEngine('pdf', PdfEngine::class, [
    'engine' => 'CakePdf.WkHtmlToPdf',
    'download' => true,
    'margin' => [
        'bottom' => 15,
        'left' => 15,
        'right' => 15,
        'top' => 15
    ],
]);
```

### Excel Engine

The Excel engine renders reports as downloadable Excel spreadsheets:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\Engine\ExcelEngine;

$reportAction->enableEngine('excel', ExcelEngine::class, [
    // Optional Excel-specific configuration
]);
```

Excel output can be customized using specialized Excel formatters. For more details, see [Excel Formatters](ExcelFormatters.md).

## Report Processing

The `ReportProcessor` class handles report generation:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Controller\Processor\ReportProcessor;

class CustomReportProcessor extends ReportProcessor
{
    public function execute(?string $key = null): mixed
    {
        // Custom processing before report generation
        $result = parent::execute($key);
        // Custom processing after report generation
        return $result;
    }

    protected function buildReportQuery(array $params): SelectQuery
    {
        $query = parent::buildReportQuery($params);
        // Add custom query modifications
        return $query;
    }
}

// Assign the custom processor
$reportAction->setProcessorClass(CustomReportProcessor::class);
```

## Report Registration

### Using the SettingsExt Class

The `SettingsExt` class provides a convenient method for registering reports with default configuration:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\SettingsExt;
use App\Report\SalesReport;
use App\Report\CustomerReport;

class CustomersSettings extends SettingsExt
{
    /**
     * @inheritDoc
     */
    public function loadDefaultActions(): void
    {
        parent::loadDefaultActions();

        // Simple report registration with default settings
        $this->addReport(new SalesReport(), 'sales');

        // Report with customized settings
        $this->addReport(new CustomerReport(), 'customers', [
            'templatePlugin' => 'MyPlugin',
            'templatePath' => 'Admin/CustomReports',
        ])
            ->setLabel('Customer Analysis');
    }
}
```

The `addReport()` method accepts the following parameters:
- `$report`: The report instance implementing `ReportInterface`
- `$name`: A unique name for the report action
- `$options`: (Optional) Configuration options:
  - `templatePlugin`: The plugin containing report templates (default: 'CakeDC/Admin')
  - `templatePath`: The path to report templates (default: 'Admin/Reports')

This method returns the created `ReportAction` instance, allowing for method chaining to further customize the report configuration.

## Report Helpers

The report system includes helper classes that handle the consistent rendering of report elements across different output formats. These helper classes ensure that reports are displayed with proper formatting, styling, and layout regardless of the output format.

### Available Helpers

- **ReportHelper**: Provides common methods for rendering report elements in HTML
- **ExcelHelper**: Provides methods for rendering report elements in Excel spreadsheets


For more information on using these helpers, see [Report Helpers](Helpers.md).

### Key Features

Helper classes provide several key benefits:

- **Consistent Rendering**: Ensure all report types use the same formatting conventions
- **Reusable Components**: Avoid duplicating rendering code across templates
- **Format-Specific Optimizations**: Apply format-specific optimizations (like Excel cell styling)
- **Cell Formatting**: Apply field formatters consistently across different outputs
- **Layout Assistance**: Manage layout specifics like indentation in hierarchical reports

For specific implementation details about report types, see:
- [Table Reports](TableReports.md)
- [Group Reports](GroupReports.md)
- [Pivot Reports](Pivot.md)
- [Excel Formatters](ExcelFormatters.md)
- [Report Helpers](Helpers.md)

# Pivot Reports

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/Reports/Pivot.md

# Pivot Reports

Pivot Reports are a specialized type of report that organizes data in a cross-tabular format, similar to pivot tables in spreadsheets. They're ideal for summarizing large datasets and displaying aggregated values at the intersection of row and column categories.

## Overview

Pivot Reports extend the base report functionality to provide:

- Dynamic column generation based on data values
- Row and column categorization
- Various aggregation methods (sum, average, min, max, count)
- Column sorting
- Custom totals handling

## Class Structure

The `PivotReport` abstract class extends `BaseReport` and introduces several new properties and methods:

```php
abstract class PivotReport extends BaseReport
{
    // Available aggregation functions
    public const AGGREGATE_SUM = 'sum';
    public const AGGREGATE_AVG = 'avg';
    public const AGGREGATE_MIN = 'min';
    public const AGGREGATE_MAX = 'max';
    public const AGGREGATE_COUNT = 'count';

    // Sort directions
    public const ORDER_ASC = 'asc';
    public const ORDER_DESC = 'desc';

}
```

## Core Fields

Pivot Reports require several core field definitions:

- **Row Field**: Defines the categories that appear in rows (e.g., employees, departments)
- **Column Field**: Defines the categories that appear in columns (e.g., months, quarters)
- **Value Field**: Defines the values displayed at row/column intersections (e.g., sales, hours)
- **Total Value Field**: Defines how totals are displayed (optional, customizable)

## Configuration Methods

### Setting Core Fields

```php
// Set the field used for row labels
$report->setRowField(
    StringField::new('employer_name')
        ->setLabel('Employer')
);

// Set the field used for column headers
$report->setColumnField(
    NumericField::new('month')
        ->setLabel('Month')
        ->setTextAlign('right')
);

// Set the field used for cell values
$report->setValueField(
    NumericField::new('hours')
        ->setLabel('Hours')
        ->setTextAlign('right')
);

// Set the field used for total values (optional)
$report->setTotalValueField(
    NumericField::new('SumOfHours')
        ->setLabel('Total Hours')
        ->setTextAlign('right')
);
```

### Aggregation Functions

Choose how cell values are aggregated when multiple records match the same row/column criteria:

```php
// Sum all matching values (default)
$report->setAggregateFunction(PivotReport::AGGREGATE_SUM);

// Calculate average of matching values
$report->setAggregateFunction(PivotReport::AGGREGATE_AVG);

// Get minimum value from matching values
$report->setAggregateFunction(PivotReport::AGGREGATE_MIN);

// Get maximum value from matching values
$report->setAggregateFunction(PivotReport::AGGREGATE_MAX);

// Count the number of matching records
$report->setAggregateFunction(PivotReport::AGGREGATE_COUNT);
```

### Column Ordering

Control how columns are sorted in the report:

```php
// Order columns by a specific field (typically the column field's property)
// In ascending order (default)
$report->setColumnOrder('month', PivotReport::ORDER_ASC);

// In descending order
$report->setColumnOrder('month', PivotReport::ORDER_DESC);
```

### Predefined Column Values

Ensure specific columns always appear in the report, even if no data exists for them:

```php
// Always include months 1-12 as columns
$report->setPredefinedColumnValues(range(1, 12));

// Custom column values
$report->setPredefinedColumnValues(['North', 'South', 'East', 'West']);
```

## Data Processing

The `processData()` method transforms raw query data into the pivot format:

1. Extracts unique row and column values
2. Applies column ordering if specified
3. Aggregates values at each row/column intersection
4. Calculates row and column totals
5. Formats data for rendering

## Implementation Example

Here's a complete example of a custom Pivot Report:

```php
class HoursReport extends PivotReport
{
    public function __construct()
    {
        parent::__construct();
        $this->setTitle('Hours Worked by Employer');
        $this->setPredefinedColumnValues(range(1, 12));

        // Set custom query builder
        $this->setQueryBuilder(function (SelectQuery $query, array $params): SelectQuery {
            return $query->find('employerHoursReport');
        });

        // Define core fields
        $this->setRowField(
            StringField::new('employer_name')
                ->setLabel('Employer')
        );

        $this->setColumnField(
            NumericField::new('month')
                ->setLabel('Month')
                ->setTextAlign('right')
        );

        $this->setValueField(
            NumericField::new('hours')
                ->setLabel('Hours')
                ->setTextAlign('right')
        );

        $this->setTotalValueField(
            NumericField::new('SumOfHours')
                ->setLabel('Total Hours')
                ->setTextAlign('right')
                ->setLabelFormatter(new CustomLabelFormatter())
        );

        // Use sum aggregation (default)
        $this->setAggregateFunction(PivotReport::AGGREGATE_SUM);

        // Order columns numerically
        $this->setColumnOrder('month', PivotReport::ORDER_ASC);
    }

    // Custom search implementation
    public function searchBuilder(ServerRequest $request): BaseSearch
    {
        $search = new DefaultSearch();
        $search->addField(SearchField::new('year')->setPlaceholder('Year'));
        return $search;
    }
}
```

## Templates

Pivot Reports use specialized templates for different output formats:

- HTML: Template for browser viewing
- PDF: Template for PDF generation
- Excel: Template for spreadsheet generation

Each template can be customized to provide the desired layout and formatting.

## Excel Output

For Excel output, the PivotReport uses Excel-specific formatters to handle cell styling and aggregation formatting. See the [Excel Formatters](ExcelFormatters.md) page for more details.

---

# Table Reports

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/Reports/TableReports.md

# Table Reports

Table reports provide a simple tabular view of data without grouping. They're useful for straightforward data presentation.

## Table of Contents
- [Overview](#overview)
- [Creating a Table Report](#creating-a-table-report)
- [Defining Fields](#defining-fields)
- [Configuring the Report](#configuring-the-report)
- [Query Building](#query-building)
- [Total Fields](#total-fields)
- [Data Processing](#data-processing)
- [Streaming Data](#streaming-data)
- [Report Styles](#report-styles)
- [Dynamic Content](#dynamic-content)
- [Example](#example)

## Overview

Table reports extend the `TableReport` base class and implement a simple field-based reporting structure. They:
- Display data in a tabular format
- Support filtering and sorting
- Provide stream-based processing for large datasets
- Calculate totals for specified fields
- Can be exported to various formats (HTML, PDF, Excel)

## Creating a Table Report

To create a table report:

1. Create a class that extends `CakeDC\Admin\Report\TableReport`
2. Implement the `defineFields()` method to define the columns
3. Optionally implement the `defineTotalFields()` method for totals
4. Configure the report in the `initialize()` method

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\TableReport;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\StringField;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\NumericField;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\Formatter\CurrencyFormatter;
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\Field\ComputeField;

class ProductsReport extends TableReport
{
    public function initialize(): void
    {
        parent::initialize();
        $this->setTitle('Products Report');
        $this->setDescription('List of all products with prices');
    }

    public function defineFields(): void
    {
        $this->addField(StringField::new('name')
            ->setLabel('Product Name'));

        $this->addField(NumericField::new('price')
            ->setLabel('Price')
            ->appendFormatter(
                (new CurrencyFormatter())
                    ->setCurrencyPrefix('$')
                    ->setDecimalsCount(2)));
    }

    public function defineTotalFields(): void
    {
        $this->addTotalField(ComputeField::new('total_price')
            ->setLabel('Total Price')
            ->setOperation(ComputeField::OPERATION_SUM)
            ->setField('price')
            ->appendFormatter(
                (new CurrencyFormatter())
                    ->setCurrencyPrefix('$')
                    ->setDecimalsCount(2)));
    }
}
```

## Defining Fields

The `defineFields()` method is where you configure the columns for your report. You can use any field type that extends from `FieldInterface`, including:

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\StringField;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\NumericField;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\DateField;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\BoolField;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\Formatter\NumericFormatter;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\Formatter\CurrencyFormatter;

// String field
$this->addField(StringField::new('name')
    ->setLabel('Product Name'));

// Numeric field
$this->addField(NumericField::new('price')
    ->setLabel('Price')
    ->appendFormatter(
        (new NumericFormatter())
            ->setDecimalsCount(2)));

// Currency field
$this->addField(NumericField::new('amount')
    ->setLabel('Amount')
    ->appendFormatter(
        (new CurrencyFormatter())
            ->setCurrencyPrefix('$')
            ->setDecimalsCount(2)));

// Date field
$this->addField(DateField::new('created')
    ->setLabel('Date Created')
    ->setFormat('Y-m-d'));

// Boolean field
$this->addField(BoolField::new('active')
    ->setLabel('Active'));
```

## Configuring the Report

The `initialize()` method is used to set up the report configuration:

```php
public function initialize(): void
{
    parent::initialize();

    // Basic information
    $this->setTitle('Products Report');
    $this->setDescription('List of all products with prices');

    // Page configuration
    $this->setPageOrientation(self::ORIENTATION_LANDSCAPE);
    $this->setShowReportHeader(true);
    $this->setShowReportFooter(true);
    $this->setShowReportHeaderFilters(true);

    // Template configuration
    $this->setTemplate('table');
    $this->setTemplatePath('Admin/Reports');

    // Excel export configuration
    $this->setXlsxFilename('products_report.xlsx');

    // Performance settings
    $this->setBufferSize(500);

    // Labels
    $this->setTotalLabel('Grand Total');
}
```

### Available Configuration Methods

| Method                    | Description                                  | Default Value |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------|---------------|
| setTitle                  | Set report title                            | 'Report' |
| setDescription            | Set report description                      | '' |
| setPageOrientation        | Set page orientation (PORTRAIT, LANDSCAPE)   | PORTRAIT |
| setShowReportHeader       | Show/hide report header                      | true |
| setShowReportFooter       | Show/hide report footer                      | true |
| setShowReportHeaderFilters| Show/hide filters in report header           | false |
| setShowFilters            | Show/hide filter section                     | true |
| setEnableFilter           | Enable/disable filtering                     | true |
| setFilterTemplate         | Set filter template element                  | 'CakeDC/Admin.search' |
| setTemplate               | Set report template                          | 'table' |
| setTemplatePath           | Set template path                            | 'Admin/Reports' |
| setBufferSize             | Set buffer size for streaming                | 500 |
| setXlsxFilename           | Set Excel export filename                    | '{title}.xlsx' |
| setXlsxOptions            | Set Excel export options                     | [] |
| setReportStyle            | Set template for specific engine             | varies by engine |
| setReportStyles           | Set templates for all engines                | [] |
| setTotalLabel             | Set label for total row                      | 'Total' |
| setQueryBuilder           | Set custom query builder function            | null |

## Query Building

You can customize how the report builds its query using a query builder callback:

```php
use Cake\ORM\Query\SelectQuery;

$report->setQueryBuilder(function (SelectQuery $query, array $params): SelectQuery {
    return $query->where(['active' => true])
        ->orderBy(['name' => 'ASC']);
});
```

## Total Fields

Table reports support calculating totals for columns using the `defineTotalFields()` method:

```php
public function defineTotalFields(): void
{
    $this->addTotalField(ComputeField::new('quantity')
        ->setLabel('Total Quantity')
        ->setOperation(ComputeField::OPERATION_SUM)
        ->setField('quantity')
        ->appendFormatter(
            (new NumericFormatter())
                ->setDecimalsCount(0)));

    $this->addTotalField(ComputeField::new('revenue')
        ->setLabel('Total Revenue')
        ->setOperation(ComputeField::OPERATION_SUM)
        ->setField('price')
        ->appendFormatter(
            (new CurrencyFormatter())
                ->setCurrencyPrefix('$')
                ->setDecimalsCount(2)));
}
```

You can customize the label for the totals row:

```php
$report->setTotalLabel('Grand Total');
```

## Data Processing

The `processData()` method prepares the data for rendering. For table reports, this typically involves passing a query or an array of data:

```php
// In a controller or service
$query = $this->Products->find()
    ->where(['active' => true])
    ->order(['name' => 'ASC']);

$report = new ProductsReport();
$report->processData($query);
```

The `TableReport` class automatically handles large datasets by using a buffered iterator, which loads data in chunks to prevent memory issues.

## Streaming Data

For large datasets, the `BufferedIterator` class provides efficient data processing:

```php
protected int $bufferSize = 500; // Number of records to load at once

public function setBufferSize(int $size): self
{
    $this->bufferSize = max(10, $size);
    return $this;
}
```

The iterator loads data in chunks, allowing the report to process large datasets without running out of memory.

## Report Styles

Table reports can use different templates for different output engines:

```php
// Set style for a specific engine
$report->setReportStyle('html', 'CakeDC/Admin.report/table');
$report->setReportStyle('pdf', 'CakeDC/Admin.report/pdf/table');
$report->setReportStyle('excel', 'CakeDC/Admin.report/excel/table');

// Set all styles at once
$report->setReportStyles([
    'html' => 'CakeDC/Admin.report/table',
    'pdf' => 'CakeDC/Admin.report/pdf/table',
    'excel' => 'CakeDC/Admin.report/excel/table',
]);
```

This allows for customized rendering for each output format.

## Dynamic Content

Table reports support dynamic content through closures for titles and descriptions:

```php
use Cake\Http\ServerRequest;

$report->setTitle(function (ServerRequest $request) {
    return 'Products Report: ' . $request->getQuery('category');
});

$report->setDescription(function (ServerRequest $request) {
    $dateFrom = $request->getQuery('date_from');
    $dateTo = $request->getQuery('date_to');
    return "Products added between {$dateFrom} and {$dateTo}";
});
```

The closures receive the current request object, allowing for context-aware report titles and descriptions.

## Example

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\TableReport;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\StringField;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\NumericField;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\DateField;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\FieldCollection;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\Formatter\NumericFormatter;
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Field\Formatter\CurrencyFormatter;
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\Field\Formatter\NumericExcelFormatter;
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\Field\Formatter\CurrencyExcelFormatter;
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\Field\Formatter\DateExcelFormatter;
use CakeDC\Admin\Report\Field\ComputeField;

class ProductInventoryReport extends TableReport
{
    public function initialize(): void
    {
        parent::initialize();
        $this->setTitle('Product Inventory');
        $this->setDescription('Current inventory levels for all products');
        $this->setPageOrientation(self::ORIENTATION_LANDSCAPE);
        $this->setTotalLabel('Inventory Totals');
    }

    public function defineFields(): void
    {
        $this->addField(StringField::new('sku')
            ->setLabel('SKU'));

        $this->addField(StringField::new('name')
            ->setLabel('Product Name'));

        $this->addField(StringField::new('category')
            ->setLabel('Category'));

        $this->addField(NumericField::new('stock')
            ->setLabel('In Stock')
            ->appendFormatter(
                (new NumericFormatter())
                    ->setDecimalsCount(0)
            )
            ->appendFormatter(
                (new NumericExcelFormatter())
                    ->setDecimalsCount(0)
            )
            ->setTextAlign('right'));

        $this->addField(NumericField::new('reorder_level')
            ->setLabel('Reorder Level')
            ->appendFormatter(
                (new NumericFormatter())
                    ->setDecimalsCount(0)
            )
            ->appendFormatter(
                (new NumericExcelFormatter())
                    ->setDecimalsCount(0)
            )
            ->setTextAlign('right'));

        $this->addField(NumericField::new('price')
            ->setLabel('Unit Price')
            ->appendFormatter(
                (new CurrencyFormatter())
                    ->setCurrencyPrefix('$')
                    ->setDecimalsCount(2)
            )
            ->appendFormatter(new CurrencyExcelFormatter())
            ->setTextAlign('right'));

        $this->addField(DateField::new('last_ordered')
            ->setLabel('Last Ordered')
            ->setFormat('Y-m-d')
            ->appendFormatter(new DateExcelFormatter('yyyy-mm-dd')));
    }

    public function defineTotalFields(): void
    {
        $this->addTotalField(ComputeField::new('total_stock')
            ->setLabel('Total Stock')
            ->setOperation(ComputeField::OPERATION_SUM)
            ->setField('stock')
            ->appendFormatter(
                (new NumericFormatter())
                    ->setDecimalsCount(0)
            )
            ->appendFormatter(
                (new NumericExcelFormatter())
                    ->setDecimalsCount(0)
            ));

        $this->addTotalField(ComputeField::new('total_value')
            ->setLabel('Total Value')
            ->setOperation(ComputeField::OPERATION_SUM)
            ->appendFormatter(
                (new CurrencyFormatter())
                    ->setDecimalsCount(2)
            )
            ->appendFormatter(new CurrencyExcelFormatter()));
    }
}
```

### Setting up a Report Action

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\Action\ReportAction;
use App\Report\ProductInventoryReport;

// In your Settings class
$reportAction = new ReportAction();
$reportAction
    ->setName('inventory_report')
    ->setLabel('Inventory Report')
    ->setReport(new ProductInventoryReport());

$reportAction->enableEngine('excel', ExcelEngine::class);
$reportAction->enableEngine('pdf', PdfEngine::class);

$this->getActionsList()->add($reportAction);

# SettingsExt Class Documentation

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/Settings.md

# SettingsExt Class Documentation

- [Overview](#overview)
- [Required Implementation Methods](#required-implementation-methods)
- [Optional Configuration Methods](#optional-configuration-methods)
- [Available Features](#available-features)
- [Core Initialization](#core-initialization)
- [Adding Actions](#adding-actions)
- [Action Removal Methods](#action-removal-methods)
- [Field Management](#field-management)
- [Bulk Actions](#bulk-actions)
- [Templateizer](#templateizer)
- [Links and Relations](#links-and-relations)
- [Translation Support](#translation-support)
- [Page Configuration Methods](#page-configuration-methods)
- [Advanced Action Configuration](#advanced-action-configuration)
- [Special Actions](#special-actions)
- [Report Actions](#report-actions)
- [Field Processing](#field-processing)
- [Relation Management](#relation-management)
- [Field Collection Management](#field-collection-management)
- [Complete Example](#complete-example)



## Overview

The `SettingsExt` class provides a configuration framework for admin interfaces, handling actions, fields, and formatting. Settings classes:
- Define available fields
- Configure actions
- Set up search functionality
- Handle model relationships
- Manage UI components

When extending this class, you can customize the behavior of your admin interface through several key methods.

## Required Implementation Methods

### `fieldsBuilder(string $page): iterable`
Define fields for each page type (index, add, edit, view). This is where you:
- Configure form fields and their properties
- Set up field layouts and grouping
- Define validation rules
- Configure inline editing capabilities
- Setup validation rules
- Enable fields translation


The field initialization process is shown in the following sequence diagram.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant External as Controller/Component
    participant SExt as SettingsExt
    participant FC as FieldCollection
    participant A as Action
    participant F as Field
    participant T as Translation

    External->>SExt: fields(page)
    SExt->>SExt: check if _fieldsCollection exists for page
    SExt->>T: getTranslation()
    SExt->>SExt: fieldsBuilder(page)
    SExt->>SExt: fieldAllowedForPage(field, page)
    SExt->>A: getType()
    SExt->>F: isDisplayedOn(type)
    SExt->>A: getExcludedFields()
    SExt->>SExt: filter fields
    SExt->>SExt: prepareField(field, page, translation)
    SExt->>F: setTranslation
    SExt->>F: setExtractor
    SExt->>F: check if associationsLink and urlFormat
    SExt->>F: appendFormatter('url')
    SExt->>F: appendFormatter('zero')
    SExt->>F: isEditable() && appendFormatter('inlineEdit')
    SExt->>External: return prepared fields collection
```

Example:
`````php
public function fieldsBuilder(string $page): iterable
{
    yield StringField::new('title')
        ->setLabel('Title')
        ->setEditable(true);

    yield NumericField::new('price')
        ->setLabel('Price')
        ->hideOnIndex();
}
`````

### `searchBuilder(string $page, ServerRequest $request): ?BaseSearch`
Define search functionality for your admin interface:
- Configure searchable fields
- Set up filters
- Define search form layout

Example:
`````php
public function searchBuilder(string $page, ServerRequest $request): ?BaseSearch
{
    $engine = new DefaultSearch();
    $engine->setFields([
        SearchField::new('title'),
        SearchField::new('status'),
    ]);
    return $engine;
}
`````

## Optional Configuration Methods

### `initialize(): void`
Configure initial settings for your admin interface:
- Set page titles
- Configure model relationships
- Set up default values
- Define custom actions

Example:
`````php
public function initialize(): void
{
    $this->setPageTitle([
        'index' => 'Products',
        'add' => 'Add Product',
    ]);

    parent::initialize();
}
`````

### `loadDefaultActions(): void`
Customize which actions are available and their behavior:
- Enable/disable standard CRUD operations
- Configure action-specific settings
- Add custom actions

Example:
`````php
public function loadDefaultActions(): void
{
    parent::loadDefaultActions();
    $this->withCsv()
         ->removeDelete();
}
`````


- `getCurrentAction(): ActionInterface`: Gets current action instance

- `defaultInitialize(): void`: Set up the settings with default values. This method initializes the templateizer and configures the basic admin functionality including standard CRUD actions, model relationships, navigation back links, and default action links for common operations. Could be overridden by the child class.

## Available Features

### Action Management
- Configure available CRUD operations
- Add custom actions
- Modify action behavior
- Set up bulk operations

### Field Configuration
- Multiple field types (String, Number, Date, etc.)
- Field validation
- Custom formatters
- Inline editing

### Search and Filtering
- Configurable search fields
- Custom filters
- Advanced search forms

### Layout and Display
- Customizable templates
- Field grouping
- Tab layouts
- Custom formatting

## Core Initialization

### `defaultInitialize()`
Initializes the settings with default values, including:
- Sets up templateizer with singular/plural model names
- Loads default CRUD actions
- Configures model relationships
- Sets up navigation and back links

### `loadDefaultActions()`
Enables the standard set of CRUD actions:
- Index listing
- Autocomplete
- Add/Create
- Edit
- Inline editing
- CSV export
- View details
- Brief view
- Delete

## Action Management Methods

### Public API
- `getActionsList(): ActionCollection`: Gets all actions
- `getAction(string $name): ?ActionInterface`: Gets action by name
- `configureAction(string $name, callable $callback): self`: Configures existing action
- `addAction(ActionInterface $action, ?callable $callback = null): self`: Adds new action
- `loadDefaultActions(): void`: Loads default actions


#### Current Action
Get and manipulate the current action:

```php
// Get current action
$action = $this->getCurrentAction();

// Check action type
if ($action instanceof IndexAction) {
    // Configure index specific options
    $action->setDefaultPaginatorLimit(25);
}
```

#### Action Methods
```php
// Add custom action
$this->addAction(new CustomAction());

// Add custom action with configuration
$this->addAction(new CustomAction(), function(CustomAction $action) {
    $action->setTitle('Custom Action');
});

// Configure action
$this->configureAction('index', function(IndexAction $action) {
    $action->setTitle('User List');
    $action->setDefaultPaginatorLimit(25);
});

// Get specific action by name
$indexAction = $this->getActionsList()->byName('index');

// Get specific action by type
$indexAction = $this->getActionsList()->byType(Page::ADD);
```


### Adding Actions

- **withIndex()** - Adds the main listing page action that displays records in a table format
- **withAdd()** - Enables record creation with a form interface
- **withAddMany()** - Adds create many action
- **withEdit()** - Adds the ability to modify existing records
- **withView()** - Adds detailed record view pages
- **withDelete()** - Enables record deletion functionality
- **withBulk()** - Adds support for performing actions on multiple records
- **withCsv()** - Enables CSV export functionality
- **withTableActions()** - Adds row-level action buttons to the listing table
- **withUpload()** - Enables file upload functionality
- **withInlineEdit()** - Adds in-place editing capability in the listing view
- **withBriefView()** - Adds a condensed view mode for records
- **withAutocomplete()** - Adds typeahead search functionality
- **withTableActions()** - Adds table row actions
- **addReport()** - Register report action with defined report class and page name.


Each method:
- Accepts an optional custom Action instance for specialized behavior
- Returns `self` for method chaining
- Automatically configures templating and default settings

### Examples

#### Basic CRUD Setup
````php
$settings->withIndex()
         ->withAdd()
         ->withEdit()
         ->withDelete();
````

#### Advanced Listing Configuration
````php
$settings->withIndex()
         ->withInlineEdit()
         ->withTableActions()
         ->withBulk()
         ->withCsv();
````

#### Custom Action Implementation
````php
$settings->withAdd(new CustomAddAction())
         ->withEdit(new CustomEditAction());
````

#### View-Only Interface with Export
````php
$settings->withIndex()
         ->withView()
         ->withBriefView()
         ->withCsv();
````

Each method adds the corresponding action to the settings. You can either:
- Pass no arguments to use default action configuration
- Pass a custom Action instance for specialized behavior

### Action Removal Methods

- **removeView()** - Removes the view/details page action from the admin interface
- **removeAdd()** - Disables the ability to create new records by removing the add action
- **removeEdit()** - Disables record editing by removing the edit action
- **removeDelete()** - Removes the delete functionality from the admin interface
- **removeForms()** - Removes both add and edit capabilities in one call
- **onlyIndex()** - Strips down to just the listing page by removing view, forms, and delete actions
- **removeAutocomplete()** - Removes autocomplete action
- **removeBulk()** - Removes bulk action
- **removeCsv()** - Removes CSV action
- **removeInlineEdit()** - Removes inline editing capability
- **removeTableActions()** - Removes table row actions
- **removeUpload()** - Removes file upload action
- **removeBriefView()** - Removes brief view action


### Examples

#### Disable Record Creation
```php
$settings->removeAdd();
```

## Field Management

### `fields(string $page): array`
Returns a collection of fields for the given page type, with automatic:
- Filtering of excluded fields
- Addition of formatters (Plain, URL, Zero)
- Support for inline editing
- Field escape handling

### `getSortableFields(): array`
Returns an array of field names that can be used for sorting, based on:
- Current action context
- Field sortability flags
- Property paths

## Bulk Actions

### `getBulkActions(): array`
Returns configured bulk actions with their:
- Labels
- Redirect settings
- Query parameter handling

### `getBulkAction(string $action, ?string $path = null): ?array`
Retrieves specific bulk action configuration by:
- Action name
- Optional dot-notation path for specific settings

## Templateizer

### `getTemplateizer(): Templateizer`
Returns the templateizer instance used for string substitutions

### `setTemplateizer(Templateizer $templateizer): self`
Sets a custom templateizer instance

## Links and Relations

### `addDefaultLinks(): void`
Adds standard action links to each page action

### `addBackLinks(): void`
Adds navigation back links to Add, Edit, and View pages

### `addRelations(): void`
Configures related model actions for tab content

### `addRelatedLinks(): void`
Sets up links to associated records for view/edit pages

## Translation Support

The SettingsExt class provides built-in support for content translation through the Translation system:

### `getTranslation(): Translation`
Returns the current translation configuration. If none has been set, creates a default one from application config.

### `setTranslation(Translation $translation): self`
Sets a custom translation configuration for this settings instance.

### Field Translation
Fields can be configured for translation by enabling the translation flag:

```php
public function fieldsBuilder(string $page): iterable
{
    yield StringField::new('title')
        ->setTranslationEnabled(true)
        ->setLabel('Title');

    // Non-translated field
    yield NumericField::new('price');
}
```

When translation is enabled on a field:
- The field uses the TranslationExtractor to handle localized content
- The admin interface will show translation controls for the field
- Field values will be saved with appropriate locale information

## Page Configuration Methods

SettingsExt provides methods to configure multiple actions at once:

### `setPageTitle(array $titles): void`
Set page titles for multiple actions in one call:

```php
$this->setPageTitle([
    'index' => 'Product Catalog',
    'add' => 'Add New Product',
    'edit' => 'Edit Product Details',
    'view' => 'Product Information'
]);
```

### `setPageSubTitle(array $subTitles): void`
Set page subtitles for multiple actions:

```php
$this->setPageSubTitle([
    'index' => 'Manage your products',
    'add' => 'Create a new product in the catalog'
]);
```

### `setPageIcon(array $icons): void`
Set page icons for multiple actions:

```php
$this->setPageIcon([
    'index' => 'shopping-cart',
    'add' => 'plus-circle',
    'edit' => 'pencil'
]);
```

These methods map the configuration to each corresponding action using the action name as the key.

## Advanced Action Configuration

### Callback-based Action Configuration

The `configureAction()` method provides a powerful way to customize existing actions using callbacks:

```php
$this->configureAction('index', function(IndexAction $action) {
    $action->setTitle('Products')
           ->setDefaultPaginatorLimit(25)
           ->setExcludedFields(['created', 'modified'])
           ->setSearchEngine(new AdvancedSearch());
});
```

This approach gives you direct access to the action instance with proper type hinting, making configuration more maintainable than chaining lots of setter methods.

## Special Actions

SettingsExt supports several specialized actions beyond basic CRUD:

### Batch Creation with AddMany

The `withAddMany()` method enables batch record creation:

```php
$this->withAddMany();
```

This action creates a form that allows creating multiple records at once, useful for data entry workflows.

### File Upload Support

The `withUpload()` method adds file upload capability:

```php
$this->withUpload();
```

This enables file upload handling with:
- Secure file storage
- File type validation
- Multiple file upload support

Configuration example:
```php
$this->configureAction('upload', function(UploadAction $action) {
    $action->setAllowedTypes(['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'application/pdf'])
           ->setMaxFileSize(2 * 1024 * 1024)  // 2MB
           ->setUploadDir('uploads/products');
});
```

## Report Actions

SettingsExt integrates with the reporting system via the `addReport()` method:

```php
public function initialize(): void
{
    parent::initialize();

    $report = new SalesReport();
    $this->addReport($report, 'sales-report', [
        'templatePlugin' => 'MyPlugin',
        'templatePath' => 'Admin/CustomReports'
    ]);
}
```

This creates a specialized action that:
- Renders the report using the specified template
- Handles data processing through the report class
- Supports customization through the options array

## Field Processing

SettingsExt implements internal field processing to handle various field requirements:

### Field Filtering

The `fieldAllowedForPage()` method determines if a field should be shown on a page by:
- Checking if the field is configured to display on the current page type
- Validating that virtual fields aren't used on form pages
- Ensuring the field isn't in the page's excluded fields list

### Field Preparation

The `prepareField()` method enhances fields with:
- Translation support if enabled
- URL formatting for related records if associations are enabled
- Proper formatter chain setup (plain, url, zero, inline-edit)
- Setting up proper field extraction based on field type

This processing ensures fields are consistently configured across all pages.

## Relation Management

SettingsExt manages relationships between models through two key systems:

### Relation Building

The `addRelations()` method:
- Analyzes the model's associations
- Creates tab content for related records
- Configures proper fetch queries

### Related Links

The `addRelatedLinks()` method:
- Uses RelatedLinksBuilder to creates navigation links between related records
- Configures visibility based on permissions
- Handles proper URL generation for associations

## Field Collection Management

The SettingsExt class manages field collections efficiently through a caching mechanism:

### Field Collection Caching

- Field collections are built once per page type
- Cached in the `_fieldsCollection` property
- Reused across multiple calls
- Automatically cleared when actions or settings change

This approach ensures:
- Fields are consistently processed
- Performance is optimized for repeated access
- Field configurations remain consistent

Internal processing with `fields(string $page)`:
1. Checks if fields for the page are already cached
2. If not, generates fields using `fieldsBuilder()`
3. Filters and prepares each field
4. Caches the result for future use

## Complete Example

`````php
class ProductSettings extends SettingsExt
{
    public function initialize(): void
    {
        $this->setPageTitle(['index' => 'Products']);
        parent::initialize();
    }

    public function loadDefaultActions(): void
    {
        parent::loadDefaultActions();
        $this->withCsv()->removeDelete();
    }

    public function fieldsBuilder(string $page): iterable
    {
        yield StringField::new('name')->setEditable(true);
        yield NumericField::new('price');
    }

    public function searchBuilder(string $page, ServerRequest $request): ?BaseSearch
    {
        return new DefaultSearch(['name', 'price']);
    }
}
`````

## Core Settings

### BaseSettings
The `SettingsExt` class provides common functionality for all settings. Core functionality includes:
- Field definitions and management
- Action configuration
- Search functionality

### Public API Methods

#### Getter Methods
- `getActionsList(): ActionCollection` - Returns collection of all registered actions
- `getTemplateizer(): Templateizer` - Returns templateizer instance
- `getSearchEngine(): ?SearchInterface` - Returns search engine instance
- `getTableInstance(): RepositoryInterface` - Returns the table instance
- `getAlias(): string` - Returns settings class alias
- `getSlug(): string` - Returns URL-friendly identifier
- `getDefaultViewClass(): string` - Returns default view class name
- `getFormLists(): array` - Returns form select lists configuration
- `getCommonLists(): array` - Returns shared lists
- `getContain(): array` - Returns contain array for eager loading
- `getViewAssociations(): array` - Returns view page associations
- `getIndexFinder(): mixed` - Returns index page finder
- `getGetFinder(): mixed` - Returns single record finder

#### Setter Methods
- `setActionsList(ActionCollection $actions): self` - Sets action collection
- `setTemplateizer(Templateizer $templateizer): self` - Sets templateizer
- `setSearchEngine(SearchInterface $engine): self` - Sets search engine
- `setAssociationsLink(bool $bool): self` - Sets associations link flag
- `setAlias(string $alias): self` - Sets settings alias
- `setSlug(string $slug): self` - Sets slug field
- `setDefaultViewClass(string $class): self` - Sets view class
- `setFormLists(array $lists): void` - Sets form lists
- `setCommonLists(array $lists): void` - Sets shared lists
- `setContain(array $contain): self` - Sets eager loading
- `setViewAssociations(array $assocs): self` - Sets view associations
- `setIndexFinder(mixed $finder): self` - Sets index finder
- `setGetFinder(mixed $finder): self` - Sets record finder

# Setting Show Command Documentation

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/ShowSettingCommand.md

# Setting Show Command Documentation

The `setting_ext show` command allows you to analyze and display configuration details of Settings classes in your CakePHP application.

## Basic Usage

```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show <settings_name> [options]
```

Where `<settings_name>` is the name of your Settings class without the "Settings" suffix.

## Options

- `--action, -a`: Show configuration for a specific action only
- `--field, -f`: Show detailed configuration for a specific field (requires --action)
- `--only-actions, -o`: Display only the list of actions in a single table

## Examples

### 1. Show All Actions
```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users
```
This will display all actions and their configurations for the UsersSettings class.

### 2. Show Specific Action
```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users --action index
```
Shows configuration details for the index action only.

### 3. Show Specific Field
```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users --action edit --field email
```
Shows detailed configuration for the email field in the edit action.

### 4. List Actions Only
```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users --only-actions
```
Displays a simple table with all available actions.

## Output Details

### Action Properties
When displaying action details, you'll see properties such as:
- `class`: Action class name
- `name`: Action name (e.g., index, add, edit)
- `type`: Action type
- `crudAction`: Associated CRUD action
- `templateName`: Custom template name if set
- `templatePath`: Custom template path if set
- `isModal`: Whether action opens in modal
- `forceHtmx`: HTMX forcing status
- And more...

### Form Buttons (for form actions)
For actions that extend `BaseFormAction`, button configurations are shown:
- Button class
- Name
- Value
- Label
- Type
- CSS classes
- Icon

### Field Details
When using `--field`, detailed field properties are shown:
```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users --action edit --field email
```
Output includes:
- Basic properties:
  - Class name
  - Property name
  - Label
  - Input type
  - Display contexts
  - Virtual status

- Detailed properties:
  - Display path
  - Sort settings
  - Text alignment
  - Help text
  - Default value
  - CSS classes
  - Column settings
  - Resource settings
  - Edit/lock status

- Form configuration:
  - Form type options
  - Input options
  - Display contexts

### Links (for Index actions)
For index actions, you'll see:
- Table Links:
  - Label
  - URL
  - Type
  - Method
  - Icon
  - Modal status

- Bulk Links (if configured):
  - Similar properties as table links

## Common Use Cases

1. **Quick Action Overview**
```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users --only-actions
```
Useful for getting a quick list of all available actions.

2. **Form Configuration Check**
```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users --action add
```
Shows form configuration, buttons, and fields for the add form.

3. **Field Configuration Debugging**
```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users --action edit --field password
```
Helpful when troubleshooting field behavior or configuration.

4. **Index Page Structure**
```bash
bin/cake setting_ext show Users --action index
```
Shows table configuration, available actions, and link structure.

## Notes

- The command automatically looks for Settings classes in the `App\Settings` namespace
- Properties displayed may vary based on action type and configuration
- All array values are displayed as JSON strings for readability

---

# Wizard

Source: https://github.com/skie/admin-docs/blob/main/docs/Wizard.md

# Wizard

## Table of Contents
- [Overview](#overview)
- [Basic Configuration](#basic-configuration)
- [Step Configuration](#step-configuration)
- [Field Configuration](#field-configuration)
- [Callbacks](#callbacks)
- [Examples](#examples)

## Overview

The Wizard provides a step-by-step form interface. It uses `WizardAction` and `WizardStepAction` to define the flow and behavior of each step.

On each step, the `WizardStepAction` is used to define the form fields and the logic for processing the form data.

Buttons are defined based on step:
- `WizardResetButton` for the reset step is always available
- `WizardPreviousButton` for the previous step is available if the current step is not the first step
- `WizardNextButton` for the next step is available if the current step is not the last step
- `WizardFinishButton` for the finish step is available if the current step is the last step

## Basic Configuration

### Setting Up a Wizard

```php
use CakeDC\Admin\Settings\SettingsExt;
use CakeDC\Admin\Wizard\Action\WizardAction;
use CakeDC\Admin\Wizard\Action\WizardStepAction;

class UserWizard extends SettingsExt
{
    public function initialize(): void
    {
        $this->setPageTitle([
            'wizard' => __('User Wizard'),
        ]);
        parent::initialize();
    }

    public function loadDefaultActions(): void
    {
        $wizard = new WizardAction();

        $wizard->setTemplateizer($this->templateizer)
            ->setName('wizard')
            ->setCrudAction('wizard')
            ->setType('wizard');

        // Add steps
        $wizard->addStep((new WizardStepAction('step1'))
            ->setIcon('fa fa-user')
            ->setTitle('Step 1'));

        $this->getActionsList()->add($wizard);
    }
}
```

## Step Configuration

### Basic Step Setup

```php
// Step 1
$wizard->addStep((new WizardStepAction('account'))
    ->setIcon('fa fa-user')
    ->setTitle('Account Setup')
);

// Step 2
$wizard->addStep((new WizardStepAction('profile'))
    ->setIcon('fa fa-table')
    ->setTitle('Profile Setup')
);

// Step 3
$wizard->addStep((new WizardStepAction('overview'))
    ->setIcon('fa fa-check')
    ->setTitle('Overview')
);
```

### Conditional Steps

Steps can be shown/hidden based on conditions:

```php
$wizard->addStep((new WizardStepAction('personal'))
    ->setIcon('fa fa-table')
    ->setTitle('Personal Information')
    ->setCondition(function($data) {
        return $data['account']['email'] !== 'superadmin@example.com';
    })
);
```

### Step Processing

Add custom processing logic to steps:

```php
$wizard->addStep((new WizardStepAction('confirm'))
    ->setIcon('fa fa-check')
    ->setTitle('Review Information')
    ->setProcessCallback(function(array $data, WizardContext $context, Controller $controller, WizardProcessor $processor) {
        $controller->Flash->success('Step processed');
        return true;
    })
);
```

## Field Configuration

Fields are defined in the `fieldsBuilder` method, grouped by step name:

```php
public function fieldsBuilder(string $page): iterable
{
    return match($page) {
        'account' => $this->buildAccountFields(),
        'personal' => $this->buildPersonalFields(),
        default => [],
    };
}

protected function buildAccountFields(): iterable
{
    yield StringField::new('username')
        ->setRequired(true)
        ->setLabel('Username')
        ->addValidationRule([
            'name' => 'minLength',
            'rule' => ['minLength', 3],
            'message' => 'Username must be at least 3 characters'
        ]);

    yield EmailField::new('email')
        ->setRequired(true)
        ->setLabel('Email Address');
}

protected function buildPersonalFields(): iterable
{
    yield StringField::new('first_name')
        ->setRequired(true)
        ->setLabel('First Name');

    yield StringField::new('last_name')
        ->setRequired(true)
        ->setLabel('Last Name');
}
```

## Callbacks

### Final Callback

Execute code when the wizard completes:

```php
$wizard->setFinalCallback(function(array $data, WizardContext $context, Controller $controller, WizardProcessor $processor) {
    $controller->Flash->success('Wizard Completed');
    return $controller->redirect('/admin/dashboard');
});
```

### Step Processing Callback

Handle custom logic for individual steps:

```php
$step->setProcessCallback(function(array $data, WizardContext $context, Controller $controller, WizardProcessor $processor) {
    // Process step data
    $controller->Flash->success('Step Processed');
    return true;
});
```

## Complete Example

```php
class UserWizard extends SettingsExt
{
    public function initialize(): void
    {
        $this->setPageTitle([
            'wizard' => __('User Wizard'),
        ]);
        parent::initialize();
    }

    public function loadDefaultActions(): void
    {
        $wizard = new WizardAction();

        $wizard->setTemplateizer($this->templateizer)
            ->setName('wizard')
            ->setCrudAction('wizard')
            ->setType('wizard');

        // Account Setup Step
        $wizard->addStep((new WizardStepAction('account'))
            ->setIcon('fa fa-user')
            ->setTitle('Account Setup')
        );

        // Personal Info Step (Conditional)
        $wizard->addStep((new WizardStepAction('personal'))
            ->setIcon('fa fa-table')
            ->setTitle('Personal Information')
            ->setCondition(function(array $data) {
                return $data['account']['email'] !== 'superadmin@example.com';
            })
            ->setProcessCallback(function(array $data, WizardContext $context, Controller $controller, WizardProcessor $processor) {
                $controller->Flash->success('Personal Info Saved');
                return true;
            })
        );

        // Confirmation Step
        $wizard->addStep((new WizardStepAction('confirm'))
            ->setIcon('fa fa-check')
            ->setTitle('Review Information')
            ->setProcessCallback(function(array $data, WizardContext $context, Controller $controller, WizardProcessor $processor) {
                $controller->Flash->success('Confirmed');
                return true;
            })
        );

        // Final Processing
        $wizard->setFinalCallback(function(array $data, WizardContext $context, Controller $controller, WizardProcessor $processor) {
            $controller->Flash->success('Wizard Completed');
            return $controller->redirect('/admin/pages');
        });

        $this->getActionsList()->add($wizard);
    }

    public function fieldsBuilder(string $page): iterable
    {
        return match($page) {
            'account' => $this->buildAccountFields(),
            'personal' => $this->buildPersonalFields(),
            'confirm' => $this->buildConfirmFields(),
            default => [],
        };
    }

    protected function buildAccountFields(): iterable
    {
        yield StringField::new('username')
            ->setRequired(true);
        yield EmailField::new('email')
            ->setRequired(true);
        yield PasswordField::new('password')
            ->setRequired(true);
    }

    protected function buildPersonalFields(): iterable
    {
        yield StringField::new('first_name')
            ->setRequired(true);
        yield StringField::new('last_name')
            ->setRequired(true);
        yield StringField::new('role')
            ->setDefaultValue('user');
    }

    protected function buildConfirmFields(): iterable
    {
        yield CellField::new('Wizard')
            ->setAction('preview');
    }
}
```

### Wizard Cell

Custom markup could be implemented using CellField.

```php
class WizardCell extends Cell
{
    public function preview($entity, $field, $options)
    {
        $context = $entity['_context'];
        $data = $context->getAllData();
        $this->set(compact('entity', 'field', 'options', 'data', 'context'));
    }
}
```

Wizard cell preview template:

```php:/templates/cell/Wizard/preview.php
/**
 * @var \App\View\AppView $this
 * @var array $data Wizard collected data
 * @var \CakeDC\Admin\Wizard\WizardContext $context
 */
?>
<div class="wizard-preview">
    <h4><?= __('Please review your information') ?></h4>

    <div class="card mb-4">
        <div class="card-header">
            <h5 class="mb-0"><?= __('Account Information') ?>
                <?= $this->Html->link(__('Edit'), [
                    '?' => ['step' => 'account'],
                ], []) ?>
            </h5>
        </div>
        <div class="card-body">
            <dl class="row">
                <dt class="col-sm-3"><?= __('Username') ?></dt>
                <dd class="col-sm-9"><?= h($data['account']['username']) ?></dd>

                <dt class="col-sm-3"><?= __('Email') ?></dt>
                <dd class="col-sm-9"><?= h($data['account']['email']) ?></dd>
            </dl>
        </div>
    </div>

    <div class="card mb-4">
        <div class="card-header">
            <h5 class="mb-0"><?= __('Personal Information') ?>
                <?= $this->Html->link(__('Edit'), [
                    '?' => ['step' => 'personal'],
                ], []) ?>
            </h5>
        </div>
        <div class="card-body">
            <dl class="row">
                <dt class="col-sm-3"><?= __('First Name') ?></dt>
                <dd class="col-sm-9"><?= h($data['personal']['first_name']) ?></dd>

                <dt class="col-sm-3"><?= __('Last Name') ?></dt>
                <dd class="col-sm-9"><?= h($data['personal']['last_name']) ?></dd>

                <dt class="col-sm-3"><?= __('Role') ?></dt>
                <dd class="col-sm-9"><?= h($data['personal']['role']) ?></dd>

                <dt class="col-sm-3"><?= __('Additional Data') ?></dt>
                <dd class="col-sm-9"><?= h($data['personal']['additional_data']) ?></dd>
            </dl>
        </div>
    </div>
</div>
```

## Available Features

- Multiple steps with conditional display
- Step-specific field configurations
- Custom validation rules
- Process callbacks per step
- Final completion callback
- Progress indicators with icons
- Form state persistence between steps
- Custom markup templates using CellField
